No, your room with the clocks example makes sense. The thing is, this really isn't the sort of story that should be consumed while it's being written. As an example: In japanese literature there is the concept of a web novel and a light novel. The web novel is published mini-chapter by mini-chapter online. The lightnovel is published volume by volume, and is oftentimes a rewrite of the world novel. And those aren't even close to the level of complexity that LiL has.

For as a good of an outline that Selebus might have for his story, there is absolutely no way he'll be able to reach the end of it all and don't rewrite it, that's just common sense. No serious writer finished his work and then went to publish it without having people look at it, let it rest for a while, and then rewrite a lot of stuff.

It's certainly a good thing to experience LiL as it's being written, but I guess we just have to accept that he'll keep tweaking what's written from time to time rather than wait to do it at the end (especially supernatural stuff). I'm not sure I would go so far as retconning though. Although there is a dissonance between chapter 1 and the latest chapters for sure.

I do wish for when we get the final version of the game for everything supernatural to be more, for the lack of a better word, even. Which is I think what he did for the room with the clocks. The first version was basically, as is with most of chapter 1, about Sekai. Then the new version became about (hopefully) every stage of the game to come. We'll see.

Omfg! I just had the craziest revelation just now! Remember that post that confirmed Tsubasa was more important than we give her credit for? Well I'm pretty sure she's literally the narrator at the end of the first Beach Vacation. Just look:

Click to expand...
I went back through some more events to find additional evidence for narrator Tsubasa, and I think that there is a lot there.

Before I get to that, let me share my current theory on the narrators in Chapter 1.
I think there are two main narrators, who I will label N1 and N2, and Himawari also appears a secondary narrator.
  • N1 narrates the major events before the first reset ("Every Day I Grow", "O World (In Our Final Moments)", and "Rewrite". Possibly also appears in "I See You" and narrates the start of "How I Feel"). I think N1 is some version of Maya, but there's still some weirdness there, and in particular some evidence that the narrator could also be connected to Ami (dare I suggest USER4 = Maya + Ami again?). It's also possible that I'm wrong and the first two events are narrated by Himawari, with someone else narrating "Rewrite", but I don't think so.
  • N2 narrates the major events after the first reset, with the exception of "Trinity pt. III" which is Pareidolia pretending to be a narrator. These are "Cursed Birds", the beach events, the halloween events, and "There is Nothing". I'm pretty sure N2 is Tsubasa. She might be under the influence of (but not under control of) Pareidolia/Sekai/The World Itself.
  • Himawari has a few scattered events ("Slumber Party" and probably the dojo events). She might be the one responsible for giving us the summaries at the ends of events, or that could be a mix of narrators or just Selebus himself.
If DeSkel15 is correct about there being three narrators (which makes sense to me), these three should continue being the narrators for the remaining chapters. I'm interested to see if there continues to be a "primary narrator" which only switches at resets. The switch doesn't happen every time; N2 still narrates in the first half of Chapter 2 for at least the onsen event.

I'm going to make a post at some point about the identity of N1, but it won't be before 0.41 and I might end up holding off until I finish my playthrough.

OK, on to why I think N2 is Tsubasa. I already talked about "Cursed Birds" and the beach events in a previous post, which I'll link here.
aramaug said:
Great catch. Given the identical wording, I think we have to assume that either Tsubasa is the narrator or is very closely connected to whoever is.

I actually think Tsubasa fits really well with what we know about the (first) beach narrator. As I posted previously, the stuff the narrator says about the tree indicates that they want to become a god or at least godlike.
View attachment 3770737
View attachment 3770738
View attachment 3770739
Earlier in the event, the narrator indicates that they are unhappy with the "God god" who made the world. They want their own world where they can do what they want, which includes helping their loved ones.
View attachment 3770790
View attachment 3770796
The narrator also seems to have empathy for the girls, which I think rules out Sekai/Pareidolia/The World Itself.

All of that seems very consistent with what we know about Tsubasa's motivations, wanting to have the power to manipulate people for benevolent reasons. In "Playing God" she even states that she wants to fill the role of a god who isn't doing their job.
View attachment 3770805
View attachment 3770809


Prior to the beach vacation, the "Cursded Birds" event opens with a monologue that I originally thought was just Sensei, but it actually makes a lot of sense that it's introducing Tsubasa as a new narrator. This is how the event opens:
View attachment 3770825
The opening line is exactly the same as the game's first event ("Every Day I Grow Some More"). However, this time there is a different "first thing" that the narrator doesn't understand, so it's almost certainly a different narrator. I think the repeat of Narrator #1's opening line is meant to indicate a Narrator #2 is now introducing themselves. Also note that the narrator is describing the difference between childhood and adulthood, which implies they have a fair bit of experience with being an adult.

After that, the narrator starts talking about manipulation, which they seem to view as something that helps people
View attachment 3770852
And the monologue closes with an indictment of "God god", which I think is the only time outside of the beach vacation that a narrator uses that term in Chapter 1.
View attachment 3770856
So in summary: possibly a new narrator, is/was an adult, views manipulation as a tool for good, and uses the same language as the beach narrator. Tsubasa seems like a perfect fit.


As for how Tsubasa is able to act as a narrator, I suspect it has something to do with the wishing well (or if Tsubasa isn't the narrator, that's how they're connected).
The beach narrator wants Sensei to throw himself into the wishing well.
View attachment 3770866
The last things that the Xoanon shows us in "Mother's Milk" is the Tsukioka manor sakura tree.
View attachment 3770867
The Xoanon calls Sensei a puppet and says that others want to use him for purposes that the Xoanon agrees with. This could just be the gods, but Tsubasa has explicitly referred to Sensei as her puppet.
View attachment 3770870
View attachment 3770871
View attachment 3770873
View attachment 3770874
View attachment 3770875
The beach narrator tells Sensei he can see more with his eyes closed, and the Xoanon says his eyes are closed to avoid being blinded.
View attachment 3770885
View attachment 3770886
View attachment 3770888
Makoto says the same thing about seeing with your eyes closed in "Bluejay", and there's a good chance that she enters the wishing well since she gets Sensei's eyes. She says it before the suicide, however. Maybe she already has a wishing well connection from doing the same thing in previous resets, I'm not sure.

Edit: Oh and I forgot to mention, the beach narrator talks a lot about ticking clocks (and Rin starts hearing them). The room with clocks might be in the wishing well.
Click to expand...
And here's her other Chapter 1 narration and additional evidence I've found.
First, there is another event where Tsubasa word-for-word repeats something that she wasn't present for. This time she's quoting Maya.



You could probably come up with a lot of meanings for this, but my interpretation is that Selebus is highlighting how the two narrators are using the same methods to try to achieve different goals: I think N1/Maya wants Sensei to fix the world (probably ending all of the supernatural shit), and N2/Tsubasa wants Sensei to take control of the world in order to help people.

The Halloween events are probably the same narrator as the beach due to a similarity in tone, content, and sharing what I think is a particular quirk of N2: they almost never refer to the girls by name, instead saying things like "a girl" or "this girl". In the event "Pry With a Smile", the narrator suggests the effectiveness of doing what it says in the title: prying is received better when you're smiling.

But in the scene, no one is smiling, and of course Sensei never smiles. So who is the one who pries with a smile? There is one character who constantly uses this tactic: Tsubasa. Just some of the many examples:












I'm not going to go into detail on "There is Nothing", but the narrator suggests Sensei become God, expresses their relationship with Sensei in terms of friendship instead of love, and forces him to do something because it's for the best. These are all consistent with the beach narrator/Tsubasa.

Chika's Chapter 2 onsen trip is narrated by the same person as Chapter 1 Halloween. Again, they have the same quirk of not using girls' names, and they talk about Chika's goosebumps in both events.


The narrator says that they are personally affected by the "mixture of temperatures" in the scene, suggesting that they are physically experiencing the onsen. And right after the narrator stops talking, Tsubasa shows up.



There are some events later in the game that make more sense to me if Tsubasa is a narrator. In Chapter 4, a narrator (maybe N1; unlike N2, this narrator often uses full names, e.g. "Tsukasa Tsukioka" in this event) describes the Tsukioka family and seems to really dislike Tsubasa.



The sludge is another reason to suspect a connection to The World Itself/Sekai/Pareidolia.
The narrator goes on to talk about Tsubasa's motivations, but says they might have been lied to.

The reason this is so interesting is because normally the narrators seem to have direct access to the girls' mental states, thoughts, secrets, etc. For example, in this same event the narrator talks about what Touka and Tsukasa are thinking. On the other hand, the narrator only knows about what Tsubasa wants because someone has told them about it. Something makes Tsubasa special so that the narrator can't directly access her thoughts. And given the narrator is worried about being lied to, maybe the person who told them was Tsubasa herself, the exceptional liar.

I think this is explained by two rival narrators who can't use their full powers with respect to each other. If the rival narrator is actually Maya, it would interesting to see her and Tsubasa interact. Unfortunately, that still hasn't happened (and may no longer be meaningful, depending how much New Maya knows).

One last piece of evidence: during one of her prying sessions, Tsubasa asks Sensei if it's possible to love someone if they're always right beside you, which causes him to think about Maya (probably).

I think language like this is used to refer to the narrators, who are always with Sensei. Hence why he thinks about Maya, the other narrator. But I think she's actually asking whether it's possible for her to love Sensei (and/or the other way around) despite always being with him as a narrator.

There were other correspondences I found between the attitudes of N2 and Tsubasa, but this post is already long enough so I'll stop here.

Before I get to that, let me share my current theory on the narrators in Chapter 1.
Spoiler
I think there are two main narrators, who I will label N1 and N2, and Himawari also appears a secondary narrator.
N1 narrates the major events before the first reset ("Every Day I Grow", "O World (In Our Final Moments)", and "Rewrite". Possibly also appears in "I See You" and narrates the start of "How I Feel"). I think N1 is some version of Maya, but there's still some weirdness there, and in particular some evidence that the narrator could also be connected to Ami (dare I suggest
USER4 = Maya + Ami
again?). It's also possible that I'm wrong and the first two events are narrated by Himawari, with someone else narrating "Rewrite", but I don't think so.
N2 narrates the major events after the first reset, with the exception of "Trinity pt. III" which is Pareidolia pretending to be a narrator. These are "Cursed Birds", the beach events, the halloween events, and "There is Nothing". I'm pretty sure N2 is Tsubasa. She might be under the influence of (but not under control of) Pareidolia/Sekai/The World Itself.
Himawari has a few scattered events ("Slumber Party" and probably the dojo events). She might be the one responsible for giving us the summaries at the ends of events, or that could be a mix of narrators or just Selebus himself.
If
DeSkel15

I'm interested to see if there continues to be a "primary narrator" which only switches at resets. The switch doesn't happen every time; N2 still narrates in the first half of Chapter 2 for at least the onsen event.
I'm going to make a post at some point about the identity of N1, but it won't be before 0.41 and I might end up holding off until I finish my playthrough.

From the very beginning Tsubasa was "Manipulative in a good way" as Akira puts it,which i dont disagree with per say.Moving on now is the time to make some leaps.When we first visited her mansion she spoke(and was very proud about) the mansions garden.She rambled on and on about its great history and whatnot but she said something that caught my attention.
I I find this particularly weird.You are telling me that the richest,most powerful family in Kumon-mi allowed something to happen to their garden?I find that unlickely.So time to strech.

Lets talk about Yasus religion.We know very little about her religion.It borrows certain characteristics from older ones and its decently old.Older than 200 years that is and it originated here.Now the strech.It sounds very 90s Hollywood super-villain ish but hear me out.Time and time again the "Wishing Well' has been mentioned.The wishing well,in its most literal definition is a device that can grant you ANY wish,no matter how impropable it may seem.So my strech is this.

Yasus religion,while old has very very few-or perhaps only one-followers.There is no text,no official church,no holy book.There is nothing other than its age and "Mysticism" that can help us call it a religion.So i decided to call it a cult.Yasus religion was a cult,founded first by the original {inser tsubasa family name} head in order to reach the wishing well.Of course as the Heads changed and time passed each Head wanted something different from it.Some could have wanted for the family to flourish,for eternal life,for riches.It matters not.Now i believe that Tsubasas wish is to remake the world to her every need.To make a "perfect world" since God hasnt come out to help.To double down on this theory of mine i believe that for whatever reason Akira is needed.For what? i cannot know.But from Tsubasas track record we know she is a very smart,cold and calculating person.She never does something just because she felt like it.So she has her reasons for appraoching us.

Anyways thats the funny thought experiment.Knock yourselves out.

My take is that most of these "Narrators" are just products of Akiras psycosis.Him thinking this whole world is a game,his blackouts,him quite literally reffering to "Us" from the very beginning of the game.Textbook schizophrenia.But until we get some more proof ill keep my mouth shut.
Click to expand...
Everything in this game could be considered his psychosis, but then there'd be no point (in my personal taste regarding the narrative).

Also, as you said (regarding most), Himawari is a confirmed narrator.
And since she says she's "a" one, or "the" one, depending on your preferences, one could assume there is at least one more narrator other than Akira (she's definitely not "the" in terms of being the sole one because there are multiple examples of narrators acting in a way that's just not her - like using classic poetry).

We also know Pareidolia is a narrator, and one could say "well, he's literally a voice inside Akira's head", and they'd be correct, but Pareidolia has also been messing/saving Sana and her mom without Akira's presence. So to say Pareidolia is a product of his psychosis would be to say the entire game is a hallucination, and there's no one there besides Akira.

My take is that most likely other narrators aside from Himawari and Paredolia exist as actual entities. aramaug has been putting a strong case for Tsubasa, that I haven't really bought into, but I can't deny the evidence either.

A random thought I had today: I know there's a lot we love about this game. And if I asked for some favorite moments we'd overlap in a multitude of ways. So what I'm asking is not your favorite moment, but the most unexpected moment in which you realised how you love this game.

My example will make this clearer:
It's one thing for a story to be great when you have complex and important moments, like Maya confessing her feelings, or Akira smiling at his daughter, or Chika's mom looking at her house full of life again from the portrait - there are countless of them.

But it's rare even among great stories to be able to pull off "THIS CHICKEN SAVED YOUR LIFE!" and have you so into it that you not only take it seriously, but find it a great moment. So that's one of mine, what is a random/silly/unexpected moment for you that you loved about LiL? (or realised just how much into the game you were?)

Why are you guys so fixated in there being narrators? there's no narrators, some "people" and "users" just get into Akira's head and start whispering words to him.
That is not a narrator.
Click to expand...
The thing is, that Sel is also a narrator.
Why would HE whisper into his own creations heads? Not that i think it's impossible but very unlikely.

Another thing is, that for ambiguous/unknown characters Sel uses a standard color for their name in renpy, which is a reddish tone.
Now, Sel uses for himself but interestingly also for Sekai an identical red color value different from the standard one.

/e

For refenrence: red in HexDec is #ff0000

Those get the standard reddish color:
define seven = Character("73 65 6b 61 69")

Different from, lets just take Maya:
define m = Character("Maya", color="#18b500", who_outlines=[(absolute(2.5), "#000", absolute(0), absolute(0))])

Now Sel and Sekai and a parrot?
define se = Character("Sekai", color="#96001B", who_outlines=[(absolute(2.5), "#000", absolute(0), absolute(0))])
define parrot = Character("Parrot the Parrot", color="#96001B", who_outlines=[(absolute(2.5), "#000", absolute(0), absolute(0))])
define red = Character("Red", color="#96001B", who_outlines=[(absolute(2.5), "#000", absolute(0), absolute(0))])
define sel = Character("Selebus", color="#96001B", who_outlines=[(absolute(2.5), "#000", absolute(0), absolute(0))])

/e2

So, i mentioned it some time ago, red moons in japanese culture are associated with, lets boil it down, desaster.
It fits for Sekai given the story so far.
Don't know what the parrot was about.
That Sel gives himself that specific color is interesting and i have to ask myself if he sees himself that way.
I know that he knows that he has his flaws and whatever.
I wonder if he's going introspective there.

Idk man, based on your comment I looked into my files and I still had Lost in You installed, so I tried taking a look because maybe it is a true injustice? No shit, first save I load there's a disembodied entity called Sekai waiting for me at the rooftop.

and even the icon for the game is basically the Wires smile

The ui is basically the same as well


dorm events with the board and stuff


and some things are just... this one is just ridiculous, blatant rip-off of this town has two halves
Now, I'm not about to dissect similarities because, again, I didn't like the game and barely remember it. I'd have to replay it in order to do that, and it simply didn't appeal to me. I will say though that the reason I didn't like the game had nothing to do with it being similar to LiL or anything like that, but because I had glaring issues with the plot.

I will offer an example from what I do remember. Specifically, there is this one event where dude goes:
"Man, I still feel like a piece of shit because I was dating this girl, and so I distanced a bit from my friends. One day we went away for the weekend and I left my phone at home. When I got back, there was this text message from 2 days before from one of my friends saying she needed me cause her father died. So I rushed to her home as soon as I read it. But, man, I'll never forgive myself! I should have been there for her earlier! I should have known better than to leave my phone at home! I'm such a horrible person!"



And here I am reading this and thinking to myself "what is wrong with you?" lol Didn't you rush there as soon as you knew about it? That's basically what a good friend does, how are you guilty of not having anticipated that her father would die and that you needed to take your phone with you? I mean sure, maybe you could have wanted to know sooner, but if the author wanted him to feel guilty why not do it right?

Cause this is my biggest issue as far as I can remember: the writing. It's just that this event is so obvious: the correct/much stronger writing choice here would be: Dude sees the fucking message as soon as it arrives, because he takes the phone with him (why the hell would he leave a cellphone at home in the first place? super convoluted plot reason), but dismisses it as nothing serious because of his girlfriend time, and then when he learns what that was about he rushes there in guilt. Now he's guilty of something.

Hey, you want him to be a real jackass? Make him realise that it was serious, but whatever it was he'd deal with it after the trip. Maybe he finds out that something serious happened on the same night he's about to have sex with his girlfriend for the first time, and he chooses to ignore his phone. Then, if you really want to fuck with the plot, you make the childhood friend kiss him out of desperation and grief, and he lets her because he feels guilty about not being there for her, at the same time he's thinking about how he's betraying his girlfriend that just gave him her virginity. Anyway, the writing is weak.

And if you read the ramble, that's the problem with taking inspiration from a piece of work that is much more than assets, themes, and imagery. Cause in terms of game design, this one is probably better than LiL. But LiL is what it is because it excels in writing, and if you take inspiration from something then it's gonna be compared to that. And yeah, the writing isn't good here (although it's clearly trying to be). That's the issue for me, because this isn't a story about Akira, it's its own thing more or less and if the story was compelling I'd be super happy about it. But it's not good enough to be taken seriously, and it isn't silly enough to be taken lightly - at times, being perfectly honest, it reads like fanfiction.

Now, this is my take - if someone enjoyed the game, more power to them - I spent time in it, and I sure wish I had. Hell, I wish we had 30 more Lost in Yous, cause if we did, chances are I'd enjoy some of them myself. So I hope the author finds success in his game, and that his writing skill continues improving.

But it's not good enough to be taken seriously, and it isn't silly enough to be taken lightly - at times, being perfectly honest, it reads like fanfiction.
Now, this is my take - if someone enjoyed the game, more power to them - I spent time in it, and I sure wish I had. Hell, I wish we had 30 more Lost in Yous, cause if we did, chances are I'd enjoy some of them myself. So I hope the author finds success in his game, and that his writing skill continues improving.

spoilers.title: the issue I remember about this game
spoilers.html:
"Man, I still feel like a piece of shit because I was dating this girl, and so I distanced a bit from my friends. One day we went away for the weekend and I left my phone at home. When I got back, there was this text message from 2 days before from one of my friends saying she needed me cause her father died. So I rushed to her home as soon as I read it. But, man, I'll never forgive myself! I should have been there for her earlier! I should have known better than to leave my phone at home! I'm such a horrible person!"



And here I am reading this and thinking to myself "what is wrong with you?" lol Didn't you rush there as soon as you knew about it? That's basically what a good friend does, how are you guilty of not having anticipated that her father would die and that you needed to take your phone with you? I mean sure, maybe you could have wanted to know sooner, but if the author wanted him to feel guilty why not do it right?

Cause this is my biggest issue as far as I can remember: the writing. It's just that this event is so obvious: the correct/much stronger writing choice here would be: Dude sees the fucking message as soon as it arrives, because he takes the phone with him (why the hell would he leave a cellphone at home in the first place? super convoluted plot reason), but dismisses it as nothing serious because of his girlfriend time, and then when he learns what that was about he rushes there in guilt. Now he's guilty of something.

Hey, you want him to be a real jackass? Make him realise that it was serious, but whatever it was he'd deal with it after the trip. Maybe he finds out that something serious happened on the same night he's about to have sex with his girlfriend for the first time, and he chooses to ignore his phone. Then, if you really want to fuck with the plot, you make the childhood friend kiss him out of desperation and grief, and he lets her because he feels guilty about not being there for her, at the same time he's thinking about how he's betraying his girlfriend that just gave him her virginity. Anyway, the writing is weak.

posts.content_html_raw:
Moonflare said:
important query, is there some way to check on event's conditions to trigger through urm? (or through some other way) - I ask this in regard to new updates.
Click to expand...
The simpliest way is to read game code.

0) Install something usefull to search text in all files in a folder and subfolders, it would be handy. I'm using vscode
1) Search 'screens.rpy' for event title. I serached for "subhuman" and found this:


Code basically states "Render button "Subhuman" and Replay harukasping1 on click". harukasping1 is an internal name for this event, which used to replay it

2) Now, search for a place when event is triggered. Coresponding line of code would be "jump harukaspring1" It can be in any *.rpy file in the game folder. In this case, it was in game/MollyEvents.rpy



3) look at the "label mollycafe" string in the top. It is self-descriptive enough, but if it isn't, you can repeat this step and find how to get there


(i.e. from chapter4 "night" menu)

4) look at conditions

a) mollyspring2 == True
search screens.rpy for the mention of "mollyspring2"

It checks for "Fated to Love You" Molly event

b) day == 2
it's tuesday (monay is 1, sunday is 7)

c) harukasex == True
It is not an event, so you can't find it in game/screens.rpy. You can find where is this so-called flag is set, but it's better to assume it means that you haven't rejected haruka neither in "Invisible Worm" nor in "Roses"

d) harukaspirng1miss == False
This event is missable. As in (c), it is a flag

e) harukaspirng1 == False

Trivial check that you haven't already completed this event. Actualy, it is a flag too, but most event set same flag their name is when they are compelted

f) senseisad == False

Chapter4 global flag, always set

g) mollycamp1 == True

See (a)

5) Advanced stuff: reading event scripts to find how to set up a flag

Important notice: it might be commplicated AF and might be quite simple

Search all files for "harukaspring1miss ="




Now lookup coresponding label



saracamp2 is an event label, so search game/screens.rpy again




Conslusion: to get harukaspring1miss flag you should not have "harukasex" flag during Sara's event "I've Been Thinking About Leaving This Place"

I haven't used harukasex as example, because it would bemuch harder, but this is the idea

Well, I said this before, but there is no choice in LiL. There is only: you either read the story Selebus wants to tell, or you read a poorly made version of it where things make less sense. I missed the event after seeing it once too, I get it, that's just the reaction any sane human being would have there. But that's just a fantasy at the end of the day.
The story has to account for the real timeline where they had sex, and so therefore "your" decision of leaving can't have enough impact for it to diverge so much from it. I think both options leave a lot of potential growth for both characters. But not in the same way.

If Akira leaves, then he understands that limits exist, that it is ultimately up to him to control the voices in his head, and for Io to understand that indeed not everyone is broken beyond repair, nor her visions on sex are absolute.

if Akira stays, then he is forced to come to terms with the reality that he is broken and that his way of interacting with others through sex is simply not enough nor healthy, perhaps that the voices in his head are, as you put it, a bullshit fantasy. As for Io, it also offers a lot for her to reflect, because she went through it. And either has to come to terms with her actual limit regarding him, which is very important for someone that considers herself garbage (knowing what you shouldn't be willing to do is the first step for self-respect) , or that things can indeed be different and it wasn't the exact same.

The issue here is that almost all of the bad consequences of having sex with her have to be chipped off, cause otherwise she'd simply be broken and she most certainly would not be broken from Akira showing her hope.

So here's what's going to happen, on the next Io event we're going to have a trigger that will dictate if she kept away from Akira because she had to relive her trauma, or because he inspired her in rejecting her reliving that trauma. And somehow those two will have to justify the same time away from him, and lead her to the same outcome. That's just a bad restriction to have when writing a story.

I personally think that both outcomes have great potential, but it is glaringly obvious that having a choice here will cheapen the Io narrative. I understand why Selebus does this (to force player reflection), and I continue not agreeing that the damage the story takes is worth it.

I don't think anyone disputes the idea of a choice in theory, but rather its history of being applied in this game. Don't get me wrong, I do hope it turns out to be brilliant this time because, in my opinion, so far, every time he presented a choice, what followed ranged between mediocre and awful.

When comparing both paths of the Nodoka's blackmail, if Yumi stormed out then the following events barely make sense. If Kirin didn't blackmail Ayane, you lose Ayane fighting back and Kirin actually being human trash instead of just talking about it. If Akira was a bad homie, then the game just forcefully brings it into a stalemate between the two of them anyway, after you miss a bunch of stuff.

And it's always about missing. I have stated this before, you cannot make a good branching narrative on a game where branches only ever go one way. Io's third event is supposed to happen - and if one chooses to "miss" it then her eventual development will either not make as much sense as it should have, or there will barely be any development either way in order to maintain narrative cohesion.

That's the point I think most people are making. It's a worry about where this will go from here, rather than what happened right now.

posts.content_html_raw:
I think the purpose of Io's scene (at which it was quite successful) was to cause a reaction of visceral disgust in the player (and hopefully Akira) in regards to the way Akira uses sex. Akira resorts to sexual contact both as a defense mechanism and as a crutch to avoid connecting on a more emotional level. On some intellectual level he knows this is a morally wrong, but up until now he's never had a reason to actually believe that it's wrong. Every time he starts a sexual relationship with a girl, it does successfully lead to them growing closer and even to an emotional connection that he doesn't have to work for. Even his most heinous actions (with Ayane/Kirin, Nodoka/Yumi, Molly, Ami/Noriko) involve him being a more passive participant, and have generally just led to him growing even closer to his victims in the long term.

I think Selebus is trying to beat us over the head with just how destructive Akira's mindset is. As such, I will be absolutely shocked if this leads to things improving for Io, even in the long run, since that would undermine the scene's narrative purpose. I expect this is the first step on Io's path to becoming absolutely broken, if she isn't there already. I'm expecting to see an Io with "wishing well eyes" sometime soon.

I do have concerns as well for what Sel's aversion to branching narrative means for the future, but not as much for Io's story. I think he can handle that with a bunch of missed events until the point where the branches are brought together again when she is inevitably reset. I'm sure it will lead to a less cohesive narrative if you decided to leave, but for me that's fine. Sel is telling a linear story, but the fact that choices exist in the first place is integral to his narrative method.

What does concern me is how Sensei's character development and the overall plot can progress if he decides to leave. I think he needs to break someone with "consensual" sex in order to move forward. And with all of SekaiDolia's talk of breaking people in order to fix them, it seems like Sensei needs to observe someone being broken and reset as the first step towards what I'm assuming the dark path is going to be. So I just don't see how the plot can move forward after leaving, even with missed events and a lack of narrative cohesion.


How are people interpreting Ami's scene with Uta? At first I thought that Ami was probably acting in order to deflect having to talk about Sensei and Uta's picture, but then Uta leaves the room and it seems like Ami did actually want something to happen. I guess it makes character sense for her to be secretly bi, she wouldn't have wanted to admit the possibility that she could ever be sexually interested in anyone other than Sensei.


I need to mull over the supernatural stuff in the update more before I post about it, but I want to say one thing for now: I've seen some people commenting on Yasu telling Sensei that he needs to swim, but I'm like 99% sure that's actually SekaiDolia speaking. I'm not sure if Yasu and Touka are even physically present in "The Art of Drowning" with the way that they dissappear, it might all be in Sensei's head. If they are there, Sekai is talking directly through Yasu the same way she does through Kaori (which was probably enabled by Yasu touching Kaori at the end of the previous event).

posts.content_html_raw:
After playing the whole update and going back to see what the other option entails...I am satisfied with my choice of hopping off the 100% train, I don't mind missing some events here and there. It feels like the right and correct option to choose. The other one feels as meaningless and empty as jerking off into a sock.

"breaking" her is wrong, and not, I don't mean in a emotional or legal way.
Akira is wrong, Pareidolia doesn't really care either way, and Ghost Sekai doesn't care what happens to anyone but Akira & Ami.

This isn't about breaking her and rebuilding her again, at least not in the way Akira is convincing himself. She is already broken, she was already sexually abused, there is nothing she or he can do about it. But slowly she has been able to pick up the pieces, with the help of both Uta and Akira. Even once she has all the pieces, pieced together with some glue & tape and some patchworks here and there, it would never be perfect, the scars and flaws will never dissapear, but she would be beautiful.

Which is why I find no meaning in breaking her again, throwing away all the progress she has made. Even if he manages to "fix" her again, it would just be in his own image, a shell of her former self. His mother broked him, and then Sekai "fixed" him, but then he broke again after her death, and wizard Maya "fixed" him.

That's a lie. They never fixed him. He remained broken all the way, but he deceived himself into believing he was fixed because it was easier than admitting there was something wrong with him, and with everything he went through. To drown in pleasure than to wallow in self pity. I think if this was the Akira from way back when he and Io met, it would make more sense for him to break her, but now I'm not so sure.

After everything he has gone through since then until now, and after how much I have hated not having the choice to say "No" during Molly's halloween event and Karin's recent event, I would be a hypocrite to choose "break her" as my canon answer.

Another thing I would like to add. While watching how the "break her" option plays out, the way Sensei was acting felt "off". There are some ways I was expecting him to act, maybe indifferent just like Io while having lots of inner monologue about the situation, maybe just enjoying himself. But instead it felt like, as weird as this may sound, like he was a little cuck. It was pathetic. If the situation was any less serious and disgusting, I would be laughing and sneering at his expense, and I'm sure even Pareidolia was mocking him.

I have felt many things towards Akira while reading this VN. Disgust, angry, dissapointment, sadness, sympathy, joy, bewilderment, etc. But never before have I felt such amount of pity and disdain towards him.

I can't explain how or why I feel so strongly about Sensei's reaction instead of how fucked the situation is, but I can't take the word "pathetic" out of my head

I will probably not go back to the 100% route unless Selebus decides to fucks us over in more ways than just simply missing one or two events.

If you mean 'Nothing is Beautiful' then it's on Itch. You can download and play the demo, which introduces Yuu, Saki, Miu, and Reina.

As for what I'm referring to, it was in Kirin's Chapter 4 'Clockless Watch' Event:
Pareidolia - "your father had a sweet tooth as well. but his vice was candy, not cereal."
Sensei Narrator - "I don't remember my father."
Pareidolia - "no one does."

Yuu seemed to have a candy addiction in 'Nothing is Beautiful':
Yuu Narrator - "There is a small pile of candy on the shelf next to it."
- "I get cranky if I don't eat in the morning, so I take two pieces and shove them into my mouth."
- "Any more than two would be dangerous to my health."
- "I skipped lunch because I was still full from the candy I had this morning."
- "Saki hands me a piece of candy. I shove it into my mouth."
- "I'd replace the cafeteria menu with candy and hamburger steak."

Candy, hamburger steak, ramen, rice balls, thanking your organs, the "ssssssssssss" and "kkkkkkkkkk" stuff, talking to plants, etc, all seemed to carry over from 'Nothing is Beautiful', and may simply be related to Yuu. Who definitely seems to be Sensei's father, who apparently no one can remember according to Pareidolia.

Side note:
The Sakakibaras (Sana and Sara) seem to have a fascination with Candy. Noriko has a fascination with Rice balls. Tsuneyo has a fascination with Ramen. Kaori and Nodoka both mention thanking their organs. Etc.

I wouldn't say playing the 'Nothing is Beautiful' demo is necessary but there is a lot, in what little of it that there is, that seems to be related to things in 'Lessons in Love'.

Even Yuu's twintail fetish may have been inherited by Sensei, and led to Ami looking like Miu, both of which had red haired twintails to get the attention of the MC (Yuu vs Sensei).

Edit: Kind of just realized, Ami having twintails would probably annoy her Grandma; Saki, since she wasn't a fan of Miu due to jealousy over Yuu. Of course, that would have been at least 30 years ago.

Moonflare said:
I don't think anyone disputes the idea of a choice in theory, but rather its history of being applied in this game. Don't get me wrong, I do hope it turns out to be brilliant this time because, in my opinion, so far, every time he presented a choice, what followed ranged between mediocre and awful.

When comparing both paths of the Nodoka's blackmail, if Yumi stormed out then the following events barely make sense. If Kirin didn't blackmail Ayane, you lose Ayane fighting back and Kirin actually being human trash instead of just talking about it. If Akira was a bad homie, then the game just forcefully brings it into a stalemate between the two of them anyway, after you miss a bunch of stuff.

And it's always about missing. I have stated this before, you cannot make a good branching narrative on a game where branches only ever go one way. Io's third event is supposed to happen - and if one chooses to "miss" it then her eventual development will either not make as much sense as it should have, or there will barely be any development either way in order to maintain narrative cohesion.

That's the point I think most people are making. It's a worry about where this will go from here, rather than what happened right now.

Anyways now that the update is gone lets do a quick review and some light theory crafting.

Lets start with our best friend and little ball of sunshine,Imani.

I really liked how our relationship with her progressed and the fact that she was able to reveal both her body and her past to us was quite heartwarming.It was incredibly sad but i admire how even through that she was able to not completely break.

Lets talk about Yasu.

Yasus events in this update,as always,brought us a looot of lore.So lets talk about it.I think the most significant thing is how Kaori was able to enter the church uninvited.IIrc in order to enter the church you are supposed to be chosen by Him so Kaori being able to enter is weird.I can draw 2 conclusions.Kaori was in fact chosen(which i higly doubt since Yasu would know) or Sekai,through some weird supernatural fuckery acted as her reason for entering.Plus i do love the fact that Yasu sensed that smt was wrong with Kaori AND called her unable to be saved.How nice.

Now there were some Nib bits about Yuus candy addiction and Deskel pointed out that Yuus favourite foods in Nib(Ramen rice balls candy hamburger) are shared by various families in kumon mi(Tsuneyo,Noriko,Ami etc) which,in a way you can say that it implies that Nib is canon to LiL.I will reluctangly agree since right now at least Nib is a demo and it may or may not be rewritten and tweeked or whatnot.

Now theres this small detail that is very puzzling to me.Padeiola said himself that nobody remembers Yuu.Why?

Lets talk about Io.

Lots of people(me included) have written emotional posts about Ios green path event so i will abstain from further details.But i will say this.Io deserves better and im excited for how her route proceeds,since i can see the angle of "Not everyone can get better,some are meant to just stay broken and eventually dissapear" for her route but we will see.

Lets talk about futaba.

Now that futaba has been actively working towards improving her physique her hate for herself and her body has increased expontetially.I pity her but this is her own battle.Also judging by her scene i believe that a possible coping mechanism for her will be to have even more roleplay sex with us in order for her to either feel liked/loved or to just stave off the self hatred,even for a little bit.Otherwise my opinion remains the same.Poor futaba she deserves better.

Lets talk about Uta.

Utas first event was nice and finally gives me the proof about something that ive been thinking for some time now and that Deskel so elequently said.Im reffering to her tendency to look up to and be attracted towards Broken people.At first i thought that it was only limited to Akira due to her unique relationship with him but Uta dissproves that.Ami is generally attracted to Broken people,also she is Bi so i cross my fingers for possible 3somes in the future.

Now her second event was imo incredible.Akira finally said what i was thinking alll this time out loud.Why do the girls want to help him so much?Why dont they draw the line and hold him accountable?Such an incredible event.

Lets talk about Wakana.

Wakana proved once more how great of a friend she is(and how fragile she is underneath) once more.I love her,i loved what she did(and will keep doing) for us,i laughed at her little dig at us while she was bathing with Osako("He has been habitually abused for so long he wouldnt know a good partner if it hit him in the face) but sadly after this i believe the Wakana x Akira cuck osako plan has long sailed but who knows?A man can hope.

Lets talk about Haruka.

Honestly Haruka(and Maki) were the least interesting here.One had a scene and the other was just "Oh no consequences".I like Harukas slave plot line cause its hot and it can give me some good scenes but except the horny its pretty boring and i couldnt care less.

Lets talk about Maki.

Same for Maki.

Lets talk about Rin.

Rin once more proves how HOMIE she is.I expected her to be more,suprised? angry? but she was pretty chill.Plus 1 for best homie.

Lets talk about Kirin.

Its very hard to avoid the Trash human being allegations.

Lets talk about Noriko.

These events were quite interesting.We obviously knew that Noa-chan was important and all but the fact that Noriko got ropped into this is interesting.I havent looked deeply enough to write some theory or try to decispher what it means for the story but ill just say that i was pleasently suprised,her cucking comment was funny,and Noriko will hopefully get a bigger role in the future.

And thats the summary of my opinion of the 0.41 update.Hope you guys enjoy.

Well, that's a very valid perspective. But certainly one can read it in a multitude of ways. The game does tell you to stop, but that same game has people telling you that trials are necessary for one to deserve heaven. Himawari tells you that things have to happen in a certain order, and that she'll try to minimize your suffering, but it is necessary to some extent. Also, who is telling you to stop? And why? Cause in that same game there are many that tell you to actively ignore these messages.

By that same token, what's the alternative? Does the game stop if the players turn it off? Or are you simply choosing not to see where it goes? Does another user take control? Are you not what little remains of Akira's will and without you he'd go back to being a puppet? If a game was something else I think it would much rather be a book than theater. Your audience can indeed do whatever they want, and are only bound by what's expected of them as an audience. But a reader can only stop reading the story - as the gamer can only stop playing the game. The day Selebus harasses the people that pay him with "stop giving me money, you're responsible for this tragedy", then I'll probably agree with the culpability of his audience to such an extent.

You're not responsible for any of this because this is not an rpg, no one here is Akira because there isn't enough leeway for him to differ that much from what choices there are. There is only one true path in LiL, and the few choices you can make are "I choose to miss events". Well, is someone better than the other for shielding their eyes with their hands during a play? After playing the whole update and going back to see what the other option entails...I am satisfied with my choice of hopping off the 100% train, I don't mind missing some events here and there. "breaking" her is wrong, and not, I don't mean in a emotional or legal way.
Akira is wrong, Pareidolia doesn't really care either way, and Ghost Sekai doesn't care what happens to anyone but Akira & Ami.

This isn't about breaking her and rebuilding her again, at least not in the way Akira is convincing himself. She is already broken, she was already sexually abused, there is nothing she or he can do about it. But slowly she has been able to pick up the pieces, with the help of both Uta and Akira. Even once she has all the pieces, pieced together with some glue & tape and some patchworks here and there, it would never be perfect, the scars and flaws will never dissapear, but she would be beautiful.

Which is why I find no meaning in breaking her again, throwing away all the progress she has made. Even if he manages to "fix" her again, it would just be in his own image, a shell of her former self. His mother broked him, and then Sekai "fixed" him, but then he broke again after her death, and wizard Maya "fixed" him.

That's a lie. They never fixed him. He remained broken all the way, but he deceived himself into believing he was fixed because it was easier than admitting there was something wrong with him, and with everything he went through. To drown in pleasure than to wallow in self pity. I think if this was the Akira from way back when he and Io met, it would make more sense for him to break her, but now I'm not so sure.

After everything he has gone through since then until now, and after how much I have hated not having the choice to say "No" during Molly's halloween event and Karin's recent event, I would be a hypocrite to choose "break her" as my canon answer.

But instead it felt like, as weird as this may sound, like he was a little cuck. It was pathetic. If the situation was any less serious and disgusting, I would be laughing and sneering at his expense, and I'm sure even Pareidolia was mocking him.

I can't explain how or why I feel so strongly about Sensei's reaction instead of how fucked the situation is, but I can't take the word "pathetic" out of my head

I will probably not go back to the 100% route unless Selebus decides to fucks us over in more ways than just simply missing one or two events.

I tried to talk my way through my thoughts on supernatural stuff in 0.41. The first part of this post is just unstructured, rambling observations from individual events, but I tried to sum up my takeaways afterwards. And at the end I wrote some speculation on future events according to some of my theories which I doubt other people are going to agree with.

  • Another connection between HOPE and branches
  • The light of the moon is influencing words and thoughts: Unclear who she's talking to here, it could even be herself, but it seems collective. Could mean that Sekai is also involved in Pareidolia's corruption of Sana.
  • We are all fodder when the sky turns red: seems like a reference to the world itself and its bloody tendrils.
  • Another layer where people go when they depart:
    • This could be the wishing well, the Xoanon is the ultimate observer and says it's where "you will come when you die".
    • Yasu says people go here one at a time as they "complete their mission". I think this means the girls are going to start permanently leaving the world at some point. Maybe when they become broken beyond repair in the dark route, or maybe when they're "fixed" in the purity routes.
    • After everyone leaves, they go to another plane, which I assume is a new world/Terminal. Nodoka's revelation here makes me think she's already aware of another Terminal. Maybe that's where the info for her book comes from.
    • "I have to get it because she got it": who is the she? Sekai? Nodoka's mother? It could be that the upside-down house is in this other plane.
  • I don't know what's going on with Akira's rambling mind leading up to the hex message "he is in the room with us". I have a feeling the message isn't about HOPE. No capitalization on "he" and it would be very coincidental for him to finally return right at this moment. Maybe she's sensing Wires arriving with Kaori?
  • I've seen people talk about Kaori being able to enter the church. The way I read it, Yasu just "unlocked" the church for everyone since HOPE isn't around to choose people.
  • At the end of the previous event, Yasu touches Kaori's spider and says that her glove is filthy and must be washed. I think this reactivated Yasu's Sekai "infection" (YaSekai) and Sekai is speaking through her now.
  • Other signs that it's Sekai:
    • Akira think about being a "strong boy" and being moved by a set of arms, referencing Sekai's hands on his shoulders.
    • Close-up on Yasu's smirk the same way Sekai possession has been shown before with Kaori and Ami.
    • "Tell us what you mean": the us is probably Sekai and Pareidolia
    • The image with the rabbits has 4c 45 54 20 4d 45 20 4f 55 54 = "LET ME OUT". LET ME OUT has referred to Sekai before in "Something Everyone Knows and Ignores" and "Worry Not, the Mason Jar".
    • Yasu addresses Akira as "Boy" (like the Girl Who Cannot Breathe)
    • Akira figures the girls "left" as soon as the whale shows up, which happens near the start of the event.
  • YaSekai talks about Akira as a sapling that will take on a new "skin" of a tree after he runs out of stars (girls) to take. Seems to be predicting that he becomes a god after he ruins everyone.
  • Swimming through the waters of the fifth heaven, where heaven is just a name, and drowning the girls: probably the waters of the wishing well, which the Xoanon calls heaven and people are drowned in.
  • Drown the girls: she's claiming that they have to be broken before they can be fixed.
  • Pareidolia wants him to "add to his collection", tells him to strengthen bonds through sex.
  • After the Yasu events, Akira forgets what happened, but SekaiDolia's arguments return in Io's events as subconscious thoughts (the need to "swim").
  • SekaiDolia use the same arguments to manipulate Akira as in "The Art of Drowning" but they have swapped what they say between the two of them: this time Sekai tells him that sex will be good for his relationship with Io, while Pareidolia says that he must first break her to fix her.
  • Noriko realizes that something is off about New Maya. My understanding is that when someone gets factory reset, the other girls are modified during the reset so that their memories are consistent with the new version. So Noriko is somehow retaining memories that she shouldn't.
  • When Noriko points out Nao, Ami might not be able to see her
  • The classroom where Noriko finds (presumably) Maya Prime is the same one from "Turn Off the Lights" and "Trinity pt. III", which is described as being at the Bottom of Everything just like the room with clocks.
  • Maya on the PA describes the location as a replica of Heaven and the narrator describes it as a place where wishes come true. There's probably a connection to the wishing well.
  • There's shadows of several Naos on a net (a spider web?) along with what's probably the shadow of Wizard Kaori, just like in "Baby Finches". Not sure what to make of this, maybe Pareidolia is currently in control of whatever this place is.
  • The narrator here is pretty confusing, but them breaking down into rambling might indicate it's narrator Maya being affected by what's currently happening to Maya Prime.
  • Maya's "deer parts don't work in here". This might be powers from a connection to the gods or even to narrator Maya.
  • AmIOkay is writing "LET ME OUT" over and over on the board, which could indicate that Sekai is controlling her.
  • No idea what to make of the "why settle for three when three more makes nine" (seemingly in reference to gods)
  • We see a crying (presumably) Maya Prime in one of the locations from the happy events, which I think lends more credence to the idea that some of the versions of AmIOkay that we've seen before were probably Maya Prime with time fuckery. Especially the crying one from "The Room with Clocks".

My big takeaways:
  • We got even more evidence that Pareidolia and Sekai show up together, have the exact same goals, and try to manipulate Akira in the exact same ways. If they aren't just aspects of the same entity, they might as well be.
  • In addition to the Sekai in Akira's mind (ghost Sekai), Pareidolia is also working with SeKaori and YaSekai.
  • SekaiDolia's plan involves more than just Akira descending into sin. They specifically want him to break the girls.
  • It seems like Nao-chan wants to bring Maya Prime back. I'm unsure whether this is to fix Sensei or if it might have something to do with USER4.
  • Noriko is special in some way, as she's seemingly retaining memories and will be part of bringing Maya Prime back.
  • Maya Prime is trapped in the same place as the room with clocks, which might be in the wishing well or might be in a corrupted replica.
Prior to 0.41 I thought SekaiDolia just wanted Akira to descend into sin so that they could feed off of what he feels. Now, though, it seems like what happens to girls is just as important. They're trying to convince him that breaking the girls is the best way to fix them (but of course they don't care about fixing anyone). They want him to "drown" the girls, which I'm pretty means breaking them so bad that they're sent to the wishing well. The same way Akira and Makoto were probably sent there after their respective suicides.

Exactly why they want this is still speculation, but I think it has something to do with increasing Pareidolia's power so that he can maintain his infinite spring. Maybe each time someone is sent to the well, it refills it a little, increasing the size of his power source. An alternative is that it actually drains the well, but it sounds like if the well ever fully drains the world breaks and a new Terminal is necessary. So that would seem counter to their plans for infinite spring.

My speculation is that this is what leads to the dark path. Akira becomes convinced that he does need to break the girls in order to fix them, and he keeps doing it over and over to try to get the fix "correct".

This ties back in to an internal monologue that Sensei had in Chapter 2, where he also thinks about breaking the girls and sending them to the well over and over. The difference is that he thinks this will result in him becoming God, i.e. by harnessing the power of the wishing well himself.



Given that Akira becoming God is a goal of the second narrator (the one that I think is Tsubasa), I think this might be an implanted thought from them (the same way the first narrator implanted things like "nothing is real" and "the world is made for you"). If that's the case and I'm right about the narrator being Tsubasa, this could have disturbing implications for what methods she intends to use in pursuit of her "benevolent" ends. She might actually want Akira to break her daughters in order to generate the power necessary to help them in the long run.

Click to expand...
For one thing, it's what Pareidolia and Sekai are directly telling us to do and I doubt that anything they want is actually in the best interests of Sensei or the girls. But it's not impossible that they're saying the correct thing for the wrong reasons, and your interpretation could be valid.

This is all speculation built on speculation built on scanty evidence, but to me it seems like Maya Prime and the first narrator had a plan that didn't involve breaking anyone. Instead they were trying to fix Akira so that he could then somehow fix the world. That might also involve him becoming a god, but in a slower fashion with a lot less suffering. And the plan seemed to be working; Sensei is slowly getting his memories back and improving as a person. Albeit in large part due to the sinkhole bringing Noriko and Niki into his life, which Maya was opposed to. My reading is that, in addition to her selfish reasons, she was worried about things accelerating too quickly and breaking him again. She has a lot of trial and error experience with what breaks Sensei, and apparently the Nakayamas are able to do things that she couldn't.

As for the second narrator, if my interpretation is correct, she doesn't actually want to fix the world. If the world is fixed, the gods dissappear and Akira loses whatever powers he is able to gain. Instead she wants to take control of the world as a kind of benevolent ruler while still allowing the cycles to continue.

I do think this is all moot from a narrative perspective; whether or not the first plan would have worked, it's not the path that things are going to go down any longer. So in that sense it will be necessary for us to see the girls get broken in order to get to the good endings on the other side. It's just possible that there was a better alternative that we won't get to see. And I think that's in line with Sel's narrative strategy; we need to feel that there was a more moral alternative in order for the dark route to have its full impact.

Again, though, these are just my personal ideas and I could be completely wrong about everything.

    View attachment 3793213 View attachment 3793220
  • Maya on the PA describes the location as a replica of Heaven and the narrator describes it as a place where wishes come true. There's probably a connection to the wishing well.
  • There's shadows of several Naos on a net (a spider web?) along with what's probably the shadow of Wizard Kaori, just like in "Baby Finches". Not sure what to make of this, maybe Pareidolia is currently in control of whatever this place is.
    View attachment 3793227
  • The narrator here is pretty confusing, but them breaking down into rambling might indicate it's narrator Maya being affected by what's currently happening to Maya Prime.
  • Maya's "deer parts don't work in here". This might be powers from a connection to the gods or even to narrator Maya.
  • AmIOkay is writing "LET ME OUT" over and over on the board, which could indicate that Sekai is controlling her.
    View attachment 3793233
  • No idea what to make of the "why settle for three when three more makes nine" (seemingly in reference to gods)
  • We see a crying (presumably) Maya Prime in one of the locations from the happy events, which I think lends more credence to the idea that some of the versions of AmIOkay that we've seen before were probably Maya Prime with time fuckery. Especially the crying one from "The Room with Clocks".
    View attachment 3793238
Click to expand...
Wanted to add some thoughts on Noriko's bizarre journey.
1. Assuming Nao in the lucid dream being the same wizard Nao we know is straightforward and very likely to be correct, but I can't cast away the feeling that Nao in DEN OF THE MOLERAT isn't exactly the same Nao that held hands with Noriko moments ago.
  • This isn't the first time Nao got sent to paranormal locations, but during those two incidents she appeared to be a conscious but confused bystander who got involved not out of her own volition. This time the Nao in DEN OF THE MOLERAT is tasked by Maya as Noriko's guide. Being "a part of it" fits how mysterious Nao is, but also is in fact very unprecedent.
  • Nao in DEN OF THE MOLERAT is rendered without eyes, her most defining feature.
  • Tsuneyo's friend in light purple cap can be spotted immediately prior to the loading screen. He's placed there in the scene on purpose and I can't help thinking whether he has something to do with any part of it.
2. Why can Noriko enter such a place? DEN OF THE MOLERAT is a replica of Heaven, and the idea of Heaven is reinvented by Yasu shortly before as "just another name for another plane". More importantly, one doesn't enter this specific plane on accident, and one has to believe in it for it to exist as well.

The "believe in it" part I think is a cute throwback to Noriko's personality, believing things like some other timeline or some other world, though this can hardly be a proof and I am bringing this up out of romantic whim.

Regardless, there is a desire that empowers Noriko to find this plane, and that desire is not aligned with amiokay or whoever is behind amiokay, with the former promptly kicking her out. So what recent desire does Noriko have that pertains to "making wishes come true"? The desire not to understand what happened to Maya, but to know.

Thus a certain force in power (Nao, Maya, purple cap guy, or Noriko herself, or anyone suspicious honestly) separates Noriko from where and when she means to be and sends her to the bottom of everything, where what's probably become of Prime Maya after 6th reset lies before Noriko to let her know that something did happen to Maya, and let her keep this memory, but not let her understand any of it.

3. I am a little concerned about what's written on the blackboard.

First two are classic LiL BS, but the last one is "-ingle twin". What is that? If I zoom hard enough it looks like "single twin", but what twin anyway?

There is currently no twin in the game and if we're not talking about mattress sizes, I can't helping relating this to the fact that both Maya and amiokay are there in the room at the same time. Blending this with other foreboding things like "Have you found it yet? The paradox?" by amiokay, the constant theme of needing to distinguish amiokay from Maya in multiple happy events, "maybe she was never meant to be here at all" by Pareidolia, and then heavy doses of unruly imagination gives me headache.


(I wrote last two almost like fan fictions so don't bother looking for supporting proof because there aint any lol)

4. Some random things that lead to nowhere:
  • I am a little upset that Noriko didn't comment on Nao's eye colors. Of all the girls out there Noriko should be the few ones that would be able to draw some interesting thoughts about Nao's eyes, but she didn't.
  • Nao's favorite animal is probably not something real to us if Noriko never heard of it (unless Nao speaks in nomenclature or it's just an extremely random animal, and Noriko is not Nodoka-level smart), at least not frog or chicken perhaps. With her nightmarish drawing, it'd be hilarious if her favorite animal is fucking wilford blackhole hands.

This time the Nao in DEN OF THE MOLERAT is tasked by Maya as Noriko's guide. Being "a part of it" fits how mysterious Nao is, but also is in fact very unprecedent.
Nao in DEN OF THE MOLERAT is rendered without eyes, her most defining feature.
Tsuneyo's friend in light purple cap can be spotted immediately prior to the loading screen. He's placed there in the scene on purpose and I can't help thinking whether he has something to do with any part of it.
2. Why can Noriko enter such a place? DEN OF THE MOLERAT is a replica of Heaven, and the idea of Heaven is reinvented by Yasu shortly before as "just another name for another plane". More importantly, one doesn't enter this specific plane on accident, and one has to believe in it for it to exist as well.
The "believe in it" part I think is a cute throwback to Noriko's personality, believing things like some other timeline or some other world, though this can hardly be a proof and I am bringing this up out of romantic whim.
Regardless, there is a desire that empowers Noriko to find this plane, and that desire is not aligned with amiokay or whoever is behind amiokay, with the former promptly kicking her out. So what recent desire does Noriko have that pertains to "making wishes come true"? The desire not to understand what happened to Maya, but to know.
Thus a certain force in power (Nao, Maya, purple cap guy, or Noriko herself, or anyone suspicious honestly) separates Noriko from where and when she means to be and sends her to the bottom of everything, where what's probably become of Prime Maya after 6th reset lies before Noriko to let her know that something did happen to Maya, and let her keep this memory, but not let her understand any of it.
3. I am a little concerned about what's written on the blackboard.
First two are classic LiL BS, but the last one is "-ingle twin". What is that? If I zoom hard enough it looks like "
s
ingle twin", but what twin anyway?
There is currently no twin in the game and if we're not talking about mattress sizes, I can't helping relating this to the fact that both Maya and amiokay are there in the room at the same time. Blending this with other foreboding things like "Have you found it yet? The paradox?" by amiokay, the constant theme of needing to distinguish amiokay from Maya in multiple happy events, "maybe she was never meant to be here at all" by Pareidolia, and then heavy doses of unruly imagination gives me headache.

posts.content_html_raw:
I know the Io Stomachache event has been talked about a lot over the past couple days, but now that I’ve had some time to process it, it’s time I got all my thoughts out.

It’s been a whole 24 hours later and I can’t get that scene out of my head. Like… holy fucking shit, guys. This one was insane, and honestly makes me both terrified and excited for the eventual dark route.

The dingy atmosphere of Io’s room, her lifeless eyes as she shuts down on instinct, the uncharacteristically creepy smile on Akira’s face as he caresses her face, just- bleghhhhhh!

I get that Io is unlikeable to some people and is presented as such, but really, I can’t help but express sympathy and a desire to see her improve instead. How can I possibly click my tongue, roll my eyes and dismiss her when she endured such horrible shit at what’s now confirmed to be five years old? What the actual fuck…

And what’s even sadder is how this fucked up shit happens in the real world too. I can’t hate Io, guys. No matter how hard I try. It’s like Ami. I look at her traumas and just… get it.

It doesn’t give her a free pass to be a bitch. I understand that. But it does want me to see her eventually get the help she needs.

But anyways, in regards to the event itself again…

The Yumi kiss in “This Town Has Two Halves” doesn’t prepare you for this event… Sensei’s unwanted touches and attempts to
push Miku forward in “Scaredy Cat” don’t prepare you for this event… Not even the infamous Molly scene in “Lavender’s Green” fully prepares you for this…

Like oh yeah, the Molly scene was fucking horrible. But I was able to shake it off after a couple hours of reflection. For whatever reason… this Io scene has stuck with me… for how tragic, vile and absolutely fucked up it all is.

How Io simply gave up and allowed it to happen. How Akira attempted to utilize his coping mechanism to attempt to make Io feel good in the only way he knows how, only to realize halfway through that it was pointless.

Combine that with the haunting music and uncomfortable atmosphere, and goddamn… this event… This event might be one of my favorites weirdly enough.

You can’t appreciate the good on the other side without first experiencing what is absolutely horrible, and yeah… I think we got that here in spades.

I just worry what this means for Io and Akira’s friendship, really. Hell, even Uta. There’s no way she doesn’t find out at some point, right? Part of me prays her mind gets soft-reset like Makoto’s did after Bluejay, but who knows what will happen at this point…

I just want Akira to realize that he can’t use sex to magically fix everything. If we’re gonna be forced to go to such extremes with a victim of sexual abuse, someone he should damn well relate with more than anyone, then there should at least be a point to all of this when all is said and done…

What Akira ‘did’ to Molly got to him for months. I hope that this is somehow able to affect him in a similar way and he can do some genuine reflecting.

I get that Io is unlikeable to some people and is presented as such, but really, I can’t help but express sympathy and a desire to see her improve instead. How can I possibly click my tongue, roll my eyes and dismiss her when she endured such horrible shit at what’s now confirmed to be
five
years old
? What the
actual
fuck…

does
want me to see her eventually get the help she needs.

The Yumi kiss in “This Town Has Two Halves” doesn’t prepare you for this event… Sensei’s unwanted touches and attempts to
push Miku forward in “Scaredy Cat” don’t prepare you for this event… Not even the infamous Molly scene in “Lavender’s Green” fully prepares you for this…

How Io simply gave up and allowed it to happen. How Akira attempted to utilize his coping mechanism to attempt to make Io feel good in the only way he knows how, only to realize halfway through that it was pointless.
Combine that with the haunting music and uncomfortable atmosphere, and goddamn… this event… This event might be one of my favorites weirdly enough.
You can’t appreciate the good on the other side without first experiencing what is absolutely horrible, and yeah… I think we got that here in spades.
I just worry what this means for Io and Akira’s friendship, really. Hell, even Uta. There’s no way she doesn’t find out at some point, right? Part of me prays her mind gets soft-reset like Makoto’s did after Bluejay, but who knows what will happen at this point…

relate
with more than anyone, then there should at least be a point to all of this when all is said and done…

Fire Lord Zuko said:
I know the Io Stomachache event has been talked about a lot over the past couple days, but now that I’ve had some time to process it, it’s time I got all my thoughts out.

It’s been a whole 24 hours later and I can’t get that scene out of my head. Like… holy fucking shit, guys. This one was insane, and honestly makes me both terrified and excited for the eventual dark route.

The dingy atmosphere of Io’s room, her lifeless eyes as she shuts down on instinct, the uncharacteristically creepy smile on Akira’s face as he caresses her face, just- bleghhhhhh!

I get that Io is unlikeable to some people and is presented as such, but really, I can’t help but express sympathy and a desire to see her improve instead. How can I possibly click my tongue, roll my eyes and dismiss her when she endured such horrible shit at what’s now confirmed to be five years old? What the actual fuck…

And what’s even sadder is how this fucked up shit happens in the real world too. I can’t hate Io, guys. No matter how hard I try. It’s like Ami. I look at her traumas and just… get it.

It doesn’t give her a free pass to be a bitch. I understand that. But it does want me to see her eventually get the help she needs.

But anyways, in regards to the event itself again…

The Yumi kiss in “This Town Has Two Halves” doesn’t prepare you for this event… Sensei’s unwanted touches and attempts to
push Miku forward in “Scaredy Cat” don’t prepare you for this event… Not even the infamous Molly scene in “Lavender’s Green” fully prepares you for this…

Like oh yeah, the Molly scene was fucking horrible. But I was able to shake it off after a couple hours of reflection. For whatever reason… this Io scene has stuck with me… for how tragic, vile and absolutely fucked up it all is.

How Io simply gave up and allowed it to happen. How Akira attempted to utilize his coping mechanism to attempt to make Io feel good in the only way he knows how, only to realize halfway through that it was pointless.

Combine that with the haunting music and uncomfortable atmosphere, and goddamn… this event… This event might be one of my favorites weirdly enough.

You can’t appreciate the good on the other side without first experiencing what is absolutely horrible, and yeah… I think we got that here in spades.

I just worry what this means for Io and Akira’s friendship, really. Hell, even Uta. There’s no way she doesn’t find out at some point, right? Part of me prays her mind gets soft-reset like Makoto’s did after Bluejay, but who knows what will happen at this point…

I just want Akira to realize that he can’t use sex to magically fix everything. If we’re gonna be forced to go to such extremes with a victim of sexual abuse, someone he should damn well relate with more than anyone, then there should at least be a point to all of this when all is said and done…

What Akira ‘did’ to Molly got to him for months. I hope that this is somehow able to affect him in a similar way and he can do some genuine reflecting.
Click to expand...
I have written such a long post about this that I hardly have anything else to say. However, if we are to focus on how this can go into the future, well, I don't think it necessarily will go badly tbh. Which is not saying she'll be fixed by sex either. There's a middleground here.
"Taking one for the team" is something Io considered since the start, and has talked to Uta about even. At the end of the day, Io was the one that pushed Akira to do it multiple times, and not once did she put herself in the position of a victim. As far as I can see it, it's a trade for her. "I will suffer you fucking me, as long as you don't abandon me - I'm okay with this because this is all I can do so that you don't leave me now that you know how really disgusting I am." In fact, not having sex with her might cause her even larger anxiety, since in her mind she'd be offering absolutely no compensation to Akira, and wouldn't be able to justify him staying by her side.

Important note, I'm not saying that what she thinks is the truth or that Akira did the "right thing", but I'm trying to read her logic in order to guess how their relationship goes from here. And from that, Io doesn't really have a reason for being angry at Akira, the opposite actually. "was it enough even though I probably ruined it? Will he stay with me if I agree to keep doing this? Can I keep doing it?" - that's probably what's going on through her mind. As for Uta, I see it even less as a problem to her. Uta understands how broken both of them are, and since Io was the one that spearheaded the whole thing, I can't see her being mad at either of them for long.

The one case where Uta would be really mad is if Io is ruined from this. But that won't happen because you have the option of never going through it in the first place. So unless it's a situation where "yeah, Io is broken and kills herself - bang! instantly reset", I don't see her being broken. And if that happens, then neither Uta nor Io would be mad for long in the first place, because they'd be reset soon after.
Edit: And yeah, stomachache definitely happens in real life.
