spoilers.title: Io Reflection
spoilers.html:
I know the Io Stomachache event has been talked about a lot over the past couple days, but now that I’ve had some time to process it, it’s time I got all my thoughts out.

It’s been a whole 24 hours later and I can’t get that scene out of my head. Like… holy fucking shit, guys. This one was insane, and honestly makes me both terrified and excited for the eventual dark route.

The dingy atmosphere of Io’s room, her lifeless eyes as she shuts down on instinct, the uncharacteristically creepy smile on Akira’s face as he caresses her face, just- bleghhhhhh!

I get that Io is unlikeable to some people and is presented as such, but really, I can’t help but express sympathy and a desire to see her improve instead. How can I possibly click my tongue, roll my eyes and dismiss her when she endured such horrible shit at what’s now confirmed to be five years old? What the actual fuck…

And what’s even sadder is how this fucked up shit happens in the real world too. I can’t hate Io, guys. No matter how hard I try. It’s like Ami. I look at her traumas and just… get it.

It doesn’t give her a free pass to be a bitch. I understand that. But it does want me to see her eventually get the help she needs.

But anyways, in regards to the event itself again…

The Yumi kiss in “This Town Has Two Halves” doesn’t prepare you for this event… Sensei’s unwanted touches and attempts to
push Miku forward in “Scaredy Cat” don’t prepare you for this event… Not even the infamous Molly scene in “Lavender’s Green” fully prepares you for this…

Like oh yeah, the Molly scene was fucking horrible. But I was able to shake it off after a couple hours of reflection. For whatever reason… this Io scene has stuck with me… for how tragic, vile and absolutely fucked up it all is.

How Io simply gave up and allowed it to happen. How Akira attempted to utilize his coping mechanism to attempt to make Io feel good in the only way he knows how, only to realize halfway through that it was pointless.

Combine that with the haunting music and uncomfortable atmosphere, and goddamn… this event… This event might be one of my favorites weirdly enough.

You can’t appreciate the good on the other side without first experiencing what is absolutely horrible, and yeah… I think we got that here in spades.

I just worry what this means for Io and Akira’s friendship, really. Hell, even Uta. There’s no way she doesn’t find out at some point, right? Part of me prays her mind gets soft-reset like Makoto’s did after Bluejay, but who knows what will happen at this point…

I just want Akira to realize that he can’t use sex to magically fix everything. If we’re gonna be forced to go to such extremes with a victim of sexual abuse, someone he should damn well relate with more than anyone, then there should at least be a point to all of this when all is said and done…

What Akira ‘did’ to Molly got to him for months. I hope that this is somehow able to affect him in a similar way and he can do some genuine reflecting.

In particular, I think it's possible and maybe even likely that the Sekai in Akira's head is Pareidolia creating a fictional version of Sekai using some amount of the real one taken from Akira's memories. letting it happen
, she's counting on it happening because in her mind it's the way things
have to go
for him to remain with her. But that's
her
idea, not Akira's.

"I was already trash, and this person now knows the part of me I most despise, and didn't want him to find out. The only thing he's interested in is sex, that's the one thing I have left to give. away
from Uta. She views him as an animal acting only on instinct. posts.content_html_raw:
Alright I finished 0.41.0
This time I typed out my impressions for each set of events as I went
This event is mostly boring. I'm intrigued by where Ami went off to at the beginning. Seeing Sensei's parents come up again is interesting but for the most part doesn't go anywhere.
The rest of it is normal Yasu stuff. Cryptic gibberish I don't fully understand. Sensei begins to open up a bit more and Kaori shows up to terrify yasu with her Satanic Sekai liver or something.
What is interesting to me is that it was implied that Sensei was imagining much of Yasu's dialogue near the end. But I'm not sure what conclusions I should draw from that.
It's kind of funny. Their last encounter played out like a scene from a porn video. They indulged in porn logic and the BBB complaint is a reality check. A bucket of cold water in the face of their voyeurism.
In the end, Haruka decides she'll be the one to check in with the other businesses. It's a neat detail that the adults in LiL show a noticeable difference in responsibility compared to the teenagers. Sure what they did was reckless and stupid, but Haruka is taking action instead of hiding away or handing her problem off to sensei. I doubt many of the Main Girls would do the same.
God I love Rin. She gets one event this update and it's enough to remind me how much I like this character. Sensei and her have good chemistry. That's not me shipping them, I'm on Rin's side here. Their union would jeopardize what they have going and more relationships besides. It's nice how easily they talk to each other. They hang out for like 10 minutes and nothing is confidential. Full honesty. It all just flows.
The big moment here is Rin finding her own nudes after casually using his phone. I flipped out when this happened but it turns out okay. Seems like friendship wins in the end. For now at least. Rin rightfully scolds sensei, unearthing more of how much he sucks. Despite that, they end up closer for it. Mostly cause Rin is awesome.
If you enter 'Selebus' in for the lust name Maki will say that Lessons in Love is the longest visual novel in the world by word count.
Neat!
Maki sort of confesses at the end of the event. I find it curious that she's never mentioned Sara's feelings for Sensei as she's the only one in that friend group that's public about her intentions with Sensei. Is Maki not concerned?
Holy shit. Holy shit. HOLY SHIT. This is one of those events that reminds me that when things happen in this game, it doesn't hold back. It feels like horror. Just in a different way from happy scenes. Some big moments happen. They fight, Akira reaffirms his new perspective as a parent. Io starts getting really intense. She talks about her trauma. She confronts Sensei about Uta's pictures. Sensei mentions his trauma. These are all things we thought would happen but the resolution is shocking. Io offers herself. Sensei is extremely concerned. Io gradually talks herself into believing that sensei is just like the other adults in her life. Sekai goads sensei all the while peddling us her own sick justifications. The parallels and differences to Io's situation are both worrying and fascinating.

I was kind of hoping Sensei would just make a decision on his own and walk away but, of course, we're given a choice. My heart sank a little when I saw that, I have trouble choosing the bad option in video games, so naturally, I chose the first one and hoped it was the right one. Once you choose option one, Sekai fades away. I really like what Sensei has to say in this option. The way he frames sex and reassures Io is concise and well worded. Io is bewildered by that choice. Her view of adults is so tarnished that she was just resigned to it.
+10 Affection
After, I check Io's event page and to my horror, there was a new missed event. It was obvious that that would be the case but I was still hoping. I load my save state and try the other option.

There are a lot of fantasies involving Io. In some, you teach her how to love again and enjoy wholesome passionate sex. In others, you're just so good at it that you show her the world she never knew and unleash her inner nymphomaniac. In the darkest fantasy, you take her by force and she cries out in a mix of shock, betrayal, and pleasure.

All of those fantasies shatter on the wall that is Io's trauma. The fade to black into the sounds of the creaking bed is horrific. If sensei can get Io to enjoy herself, he can justify this choice. But shes not. She doesn't even hate it. She's just annoyed and dejected. Sex isn't meaningful to her. It's a nuisance that entraps her and makes her feel like a tool. The way Sensei is on top of her here looks gluttonous. It highlights the fact that Sensei's justification is wrong. This is a selfish exchange.

After leaving, not feeling any love from Io and the guilt of so blatantly embodying the role of an abuser, Sensei asks for Ami's presence to comfort him.
-10 Io Affection. +0 lust.

It's crazy to think that just two update ago people were questioning the writing in LiL. There's so much to gleam from this event, so much I didn't talk about. I had to get up and walk around after this.
Also great music choices and that "Five" jumpscare was terrifying in its own right.
I wonder if Futaba's smut habit is somewhat akin to a porn addiction. She seemed a little too fixated on sex.

Futaba being concerned for Ami is sweet. Futaba is consistently one of the most kind hearted girls to everyone but herself. She's developing suicidal thoughts but love for her friends keep her from seriously considering it. Sensei was also considering ending it all but the only thing that saved him was the concern for Ami. Either Sensei lacks the compassion that Futaba has or hes convinced that everyone but Ami would be better off without him. Probably a mix of both.
It's refreshing when people stand up to Sensei and Kirin is the right amount of confrontational to do that. Ghost sekai is showing up more. Seems to enjoy Akira being at his worst.
Is Noriko detecting Maya's change a sign that she'll be on the roof? That seems like a continuity error that the world would fix between resets. She does immediately get confused by the passage of time but maybe that's just normal non-induced confusion. Idk

Noriko's super natural transportation just gives me more questions than I already had. It appears that Noriko will have a large part of the story now, so I'm excited for that.
Quick aside, I haven't said this yet, but I fucking love Ami's new hair. Outfit is great too.
Despite always being labeled as an idiot, Ami is consistently shown to be socially intelligent. It's fun to observe and here she uses it to hit on Uta. Uta thought Ami was straight but we can deduce from Noriko's survey that Ami is bi. That and the fact that in two separate instances she tried to share Sensei with Ayane under the stipulation that she become the regulator of Ayane and Sensei's relationship. Seeing Ami try to seduce uta like her father almost makes you proud in a messed up sort of way.

Enough about Ami. Uta. I'm not too excited about where Uta's story is going tbh. I'm open to being surprised but it seems cut and dry. It is interesting that she offered sensei professional help though. But sensei doesn't want help for his urges, he wants to be hated for his urges. Sensei, of course, was abused as a kid and he genuinely wanted to help young people as a teacher. So it makes sense that he hates himself so much. That's why it makes him angry that he gets away with it after being confronted.
HELL YESSS IMANI.
Also unexpected foursome. This is a wonderful development. That's all I have to say.

If you read any of this, thanks for reading. I'll be going through what I missed in the thread now.

spoilers.text:
Holy shit. Holy shit. HOLY SHIT. This is one of those events that reminds me that when things happen in this game, it doesn't hold back. It feels like horror. Just in a different way from happy scenes. Some big moments happen. They fight, Akira reaffirms his new perspective as a parent. Io starts getting really intense. She talks about her trauma. She confronts Sensei about Uta's pictures. Sensei mentions his trauma. These are all things we thought would happen but the resolution is shocking. Io offers herself. Sensei is extremely concerned. Io gradually talks herself into believing that sensei is just like the other adults in her life. Sekai goads sensei all the while peddling us her own sick justifications. The parallels and differences to Io's situation are both worrying and fascinating.
I was kind of hoping Sensei would just make a decision on his own and walk away but, of course, we're given a choice. My heart sank a little when I saw that, I have trouble choosing the bad option in video games, so naturally, I chose the first one and hoped it was the right one. Once you choose option one, Sekai fades away. I really like what Sensei has to say in this option. The way he frames sex and reassures Io is concise and well worded. Io is bewildered by that choice. Her view of adults is so tarnished that she was just resigned to it.
+10 Affection
After, I check Io's event page and to my horror, there was a new missed event. It was obvious that that would be the case but I was still hoping. I load my save state and try the other option.
There are a lot of fantasies involving Io. In some, you teach her how to love again and enjoy wholesome passionate sex. In others, you're just so good at it that you show her the world she never knew and unleash her inner nymphomaniac. In the darkest fantasy, you take her by force and she cries out in a mix of shock, betrayal, and pleasure.
All of those fantasies shatter on the wall that is Io's trauma. The fade to black into the sounds of the creaking bed is horrific. If sensei can get Io to enjoy herself, he can justify this choice. But shes not. She doesn't even hate it. She's just annoyed and dejected. Sex isn't meaningful to her. It's a nuisance that entraps her and makes her feel like a tool. The way Sensei is on top of her here looks gluttonous. It highlights the fact that Sensei's justification is wrong. This is a selfish exchange.
After leaving, not feeling any love from Io and the guilt of so blatantly embodying the role of an abuser, Sensei asks for Ami's presence to comfort him.
-10 Io Affection. +0 lust.
It's crazy to think that just two update ago people were questioning the writing in LiL. There's so much to gleam from this event, so much I didn't talk about. I had to get up and walk around after this.
Also great music choices and that "Five" jumpscare was terrifying in its own right.

I think we can probably trust the "memories" that the Xoanon shows us in "Mother's Milk", since its role is to be an observer and cataloguer of true experiences. From those we know that Sekai definitely abused him and was the one who initiated it, but apparently also loved him in some sort of twisted way.

I agree the rest of what we know is unreliable. In particular, I think it's possible and maybe even likely that the Sekai in Akira's head is Pareidolia creating a fictional version of Sekai using some amount of the real one taken from Akira's memories. Pareidolia likes to pretend to be others (the other gods, a narrator) and it fits with his name: we/Akira perceive human features (e.g. Sekai) emerging from something inhuman (e.g. a god/user/voice or whatever).

[/SPOILER]
Click to expand...
I'm also somewhat partial to the idea that Sekai might not actually be appearing in some scenes, but it's hard to tell for certain. We can be sure it's not all the time. She has too much influence and skin in the game otherwise. We're even shown that she "appears" before Akira and Ami at her grave to talk to Ami, but in that case neither can actually see or hear her (Although sensei might have noticed something strange? I can't quite remember.) Is this a different version, or just her loving Ami like a normal mother despite being kind of mental? I guess I'm saying I don't know how I'd differentiate in every case, and it might be ambiguous or non-concrete on purpose.

Pareidolia's name itself it very on-the-nose, though, unless it's to throw you off or just sound cool. So I think it lends credence to or plays into Akira's delusions. If you put on your tinfoil hat, you could probably even speculate that Pareidolia is literally 'an instance of pareidolia', and that every interaction with him and his appearance is simply 'made up' because it's Akira's mind interpreting something incorrectly or filling in information gaps (e.g. making up dialogue for him despite Pareidolia not actually "speaking," but communication/affecting him in a way he can't comprehend.) Or perhaps he doesn't even exist, and maybe someone else does, but Pareidolia is a stand in to explain the effects of that person's actions. Keep in mind that I'm not actually positing that as true, and I am a stupid ape. It's a fun thought, though.

The talk about Amy has me wondering… when the heck do you think we’ll get a new Happy Event? The last one we got was “Rain King” in 0.35, which was 6 updates ago now. On average, there’s usually a Happy Event every few updates or so, though perhaps due to it being Springtime… things are now different.

The longest gap we’ve ever had in between Happy Events was from “Baby Finches” (0.11) to “Something Everyone Knows And Ignores” (0.18p2). That’s a 7 update gap if we count all the ‘parts’ of updates as one, since they released biweekly back then.

That means we’re coming up on the longest Happy Event drought the game’s ever had if we don’t see one by next update (I doubt we will).

It just makes me all the more curious what Springtime Happy Events will entail, anyway… Especially with Akira’s mind more fucked up and prone to influence than ever thanks to this being Pareidolia’s season. The same curiosity extends to resets as well, but that’s another topic entirely.

Tl;dr - We haven’t had a Happy Event in a long ass time. When we getting another one??

I think we're saying the same thing. Also the part you quoted is just me trying to understand what Akira meant by deer parts in that situation, which is his vision of why Uta hugged him, not the reason I think she did. But I'll elaborate on what I find to be different.

I think there's a crucial difference between being attracted to broken people and finding someone that gets what you've been through. Uta's relationship with Io is one born of mutual understanding, they're from the same support group. Io isn't elated about Uta's deer parts, she is understanding of it. She doesn't find Uta's perverted side attractive, or hot, or would take pleasure from it. Uta is "attracted" to Io as one would be to a pillar of support when the rest of the world would shun you. Io could never be to her what Akira can.

Akira is an entire different thing. He is highly sexual, just as perverted, and doesn't just accept who she is and her past, he gets pleasure from it. For Uta being with him it's not just that she'd be "accepted despite what happened" (Io's case), she'd be celebrated for it (to an extent).

Now, onto being attracted to broken people. We don't have enough to analyse Prince Ami, but from what we're shown so far, she's the one that would better fit a description of "being attracted to broken people". Uta isn't attracted to broken people, she just thinks they're probably more likely to accept her cause they might get it. Io isn't attracted to broken people, she just considers herself such trash that it would take a trashy person to withstand her presence.

Going back to the main point, Uta was attracted to Akira. She freaked out about him discovering her secret, but then (after her shock and confusion about him having her picture) managed to understand that it could be a good thing for her because it would mean he'd be truly cool with her past. When he breaks down in front of her, she hugs him cause that pretty much seals the deal. He displays a position of fragility to her. So she sees herself in him (which is untrue, but true enough for her to make up her mind about it).

There is no one in this game that was more justified in Akira loving than Maya. She's his one partner (aware of what's happening) from beginning to the factory reset. That one partner is revealed to have been hiding a boundless love with a mask for fear of breaking him - which he discovers bit by bit, while having to work harder on her than on anyone else. He's been shown countless times to choose her over everyone else - most importantly over Sekai's memories (which is how the whole Maya thing started in his past). He's responsible for her "death", in which she professes her undying love for him.

Now, no player has to like Maya. In fact, there are multiple reasons not to, and even to hate her. But I fail to see how the game didn't justify Akira loving her. One could say "well, I get that he loves her then, but how come it's to such an extent deeper than to the other girls that it puts him in a coma?". I mean... it's the second girl that he loved that died in front of him. He never recovered from the first time it happened, and now it happened again. And this time it was his fault even. If that wasn't enough, the one person that might know a little more than him about resets is also gone. His recovery could even be said to have been fast, considering the implications.

It also shows a complete shift in his perspective on sex, previously he told Yasu "sex has nothing to do with love, it's just an action" and now he's saying sex the only way he knows how to show love.

You all seem to forget that Tsuneyo was ready to kill Sensei after the Molly thing.
Click to expand...
And not just for Molly:
Tsuneyo - "But know that if you are lying to me about this...and you do go on to hurt someone in an unforgivable way...that I will not hesitate to introduce your organs to Gallows Edge."
(Chapter 3's 'The Bending of Italics' Main Event)
Tsuneyo seemed to somewhat watch over the class, after the Molly stuff:
Tsuneyo - "Yes. She seems to be acting a bit differently as of late and I am not sure whether or not something has happened to her."
Molly - "I...I was talking about worrying about her comedy, but...You think something happened to Ayane? She's seemed mostly the same to me."
Tsuneyo - "Sometimes, the biggest changes are the ones buried the deepest. And we will never come to know them unless we submerge ourselves beneath it all."
(Chapter 3's 'Dorm War II: Pre-Show Game' Main Event)

She also isn't one to make excuses for Sensei:
Tsuneyo - "How many more people will be hurt under your supervision?"
- "You should be ashamed of yourself."
(Chapter 3's Nodoka 'Twisting Ivy' Event)
Tsuneyo - "The answer looked as if it had to be that or 'partially reformed predator' and I assume the latter was far too specific a costume for you to wear."
- "I apologize once more. I was told that I needed to act dominant tonight to fit my character, but I saw no better way of doing that than putting you in your proper place. Which happens to be nowhere near me."
(Chapter 3's 'BONE-TOWN' Main Event)

Tsuneyo is one of the few girls who would probably do something if Sensei wasn't always hiding, lying, and manipulating all the time. A lot of these girls are stuck in their own worlds, which makes keeping them in the dark, easy, though.

Even Io tried to pretend she didn't know about the pic, which makes me wonder...what would Rin have thought if she found Uta's wizard pic instead?

Moonflare said:
I identify with Rin on several levels, she reminds me a lot about myself when I was a teenager. And yeah, she's a true bro. You can't really expect her to an adult bro cause well, she's a teenager. But even when she messes up, she's trying her best.


Oh, that phone thing makes sense. But then again, Rin is probably the one that knows more about Akira banging people other than Ayane and Maya. And not one of these are wizards. So, I don't think she'd conclude it's because she's not a kid. In fact, if you're a good homie it's kind of clear (from her perspective) that Akira didn't push for Rin because she made it clear that Otoha was her priority and, again, Akira probably is the most healthy with Rin out of everyone else.

He did push a couple of times though. She just never gave him an opening. It's just not his mo to keep pushing when there's clear resistance.

It's funny to think that Akira's class is fully made of people the school doesn't want to deal with Other than Makoto I guess. Also, I do wonder, since the city keeps moving, what is happening with the rest of the school? Do the other classes change? Does the school itself change? Do the people we don't see become stuck as well? Or it's just when we start seeing them that they get stuck?

Edit: oh, something about the Rin event, why exactly does Rin get mad? Cause I mean, technically, it's Niki that Akira betrayed there. Otoha's the one that betrayed Rin. Is she mad about Akira involving Otoha in her life again in a bad and roundabout way? Is she mad because instead of asking her for nudes he went to Otoha? Is she mad because he kind of used her in order to get closer to Otoha/corrupt her? I don't really know.

I also wonder if she's gonna talk to Otoha about it, cause in that case she has A LOT of cause to be pissed at her. "Hey, my name is Otoha, I cheat on my girlfriend, hide that from her, and then after breaking up with her, I use her nude pictures to get a picture of the girl I cheated on her with". Such a trashy person.
Click to expand...
Apologies, a little late.
Rin does seem to know about Chika, Futaba, Niki, Nodoka, Sana, and now Molly. Also optionally Haruka. So, she is aware of quite a bit. Presumably, through Futaba, she also knows about Makoto. Outside of Sensei's sex-life, she doesn't really know much about him, though. Albeit, neither does Ayane or Makoto, etc.

As for the push thing, Rin seemed to think Sensei never did, and that somewhat confused her:
Rin - "Why didn't you ever push for more?"
- "I might seem dense sometimes...but there have been a lot of moments where I've thought, 'You know, I wouldn't stop him if he did something right now.'"
- "But you never did."
(Chapter 2's Rin 'The Happiest Girl in the World' Event)
Rin - "The hell do you want from me, man? Not my fault you're not attracted to me."
- "I was just joking at first, but I guess you really aren't attracted to me at all!"
(Chapter 2's 'Friend Zone Fight!' Main Event)
Rin has probably been down since Chapter 1:
Rin - "Not gonna lie, Ami. Your uncle could get it if he wanted."
(Chapter 1's Ami 'Ode to a Marsh Warbler' Event)
But, she was more or less Imani'd and Niki'd by Sensei, in the GH route, considering he didn't push for more with them either. In other words: Feelings got in the way. BH Rin was more passive aggressive with him.

Sensei's actually rather "pushy" when he wants to be/can be. Especially when it came to Io and Miku. But he doesn't "love" them like he does Rin, or Noriko, or presumably Imani, etc. He was even pushy with Maya Prime who had to tell him that he's being extremely insensitive:
Maya - "We can't be. Not even in a 'really roundabout way.' I told you this already and the fact that you're ignoring it is not only decidedly moronic but extremely insensitive. So, again, please stop."
(Chapter 3's 'I Won't Say I'm In Love' Main Event)
Unfortunately, if he was less pushy with her, what happened...may have not happened.

As for the school:
Karin and Wakana seem stuck where they are, so presumably everyone has been stuck going to the same school since the resets began, not just Sensei's class.

Except for the girls from the school that got swallowed, including Nodoka, Noriko, Touka, Yasu, etc. Kirin, Molly, and Tsuneyo also weren't originally (presumably) in Sensei's class, but they got transferred in. So, the students may have moved around, but unless a school got swallowed, they were basically stuck.

Maya Prime seemed to think the new girls would have moved back to their old school, under normal circumstances. (Chapter 2's 'A Door that People Move Through' Main Event)
But that wasn't the case, so it's hard to tell what's supposed to happen.
As for Rin's nude:
She was probably just upset due to how sleazy and a waste of time it was. Even Otoha told Sensei, he would probably get a nude from Rin if he wanted, and was getting ripped off. Sensei, optionally, made things difficult and tried to hide things from Rin, just because. Niki is the one truly being betrayed because she told Sensei not to show others, and now, Otoha could ruin her career or at least try to.

Rin also probably isn't over Otoha or knows she cheated, so I doubt she'll get mad at her over it. It is a crappy thing to do, though.

Overall: Sensei is betraying Niki and Rin, who are basically both his homies, for more or less no reason. Optionally.

Otoha at least got something she couldn't otherwise, out of it. I think Rin would understand, to a degree.

posts.content_html_raw: The recent discussion around not wanting to miss events in the wake of Io's event is interesting to me. The choices are there for a reason, and it's pretty clear that a missed event does not equate to failing an objective in, say, an FPS game. LiL frequently gives you no choice in the outcome of events, or explicitly shows you your lack of input with multiple identical options. Missable scenes, in my view, are things that could happen depending on your choices — but that does not mean you either "get" something or "don't get" something. If you miss a scene because you chose an option based on your desired outcome, you didn't lose a scene, you gained your desired outcome. Similarly, in the recent Io event, choosing the first option causes you to miss a scene — but the current scene continues and provides more dialogue, and importantly, narrative. I'd like to suggest to anyone feeling bad for missing events, ask yourself; do you want to see the event because you actually want to, or simply due to the effects of loss aversion, and would you actually gain more by interacting with the branching path mechanic with your desired outcome in mind? (Or using rollback lmao.)

PhiloPhilo said:
The recent discussion around not wanting to miss events in the wake of Io's event is interesting to me. The choices are there for a reason, and it's pretty clear that a missed event does not equate to failing an objective in, say, an FPS game. LiL frequently gives you no choice in the outcome of events, or explicitly shows you your lack of input with multiple identical options. Missable scenes, in my view, are things that could happen depending on your choices — but that does not mean you either "get" something or "don't get" something. If you miss a scene because you chose an option based on your desired outcome, you didn't lose a scene, you gained your desired outcome. Similarly, in the recent Io event, choosing the first option causes you to miss a scene — but the current scene continues and provides more dialogue, and importantly, narrative. I'd like to suggest to anyone feeling bad for missing events, ask yourself; do you want to see the event because you actually want to, or simply due to the effects of loss aversion, and would you actually gain more by interacting with the branching path mechanic with your desired outcome in mind? (Or using rollback lmao.)
Click to expand...
That's correct and a very good point. However, that would only be the exact case if your desired outcome also didn't result in a worse narrative. There are many examples, but I've already listed them a couple of times, so I'll just focus on one. Depending on what you did first, Yumi may resist Nodoka's blackmail or not. You can say "well, I'd rather have a timeline where Yumi wasn't sexually assaulted by Nodoka", I don't mind "missing" whatever would come from that because I'd rather have a world where it didn't happen at all. That's perfectly acceptable in theory. But the issue is that Selebus wants to tell a story where it happened.

If you have the blackmail not happen, then Yumi reacts to Nodoka and especially Akira in a way that borders bizarre. Akira would have literally found her in the baths, offered his shirt to her, she'd have rejected it for god knows what reason, and that would have been it. It makes no sense for Yumi to despise him in the same way from both "I can't believe you'd have sex with Nodoka when you already have Chika" and "I can't believe you'd watch while someone sexually assaulted me without doing anything, and then go on to cum in her mouth in front of me".

I agree with your point in theory, and hey, I can only speak for myself, but I couldn't care less how someone else chose to play the game. Miss everything, miss nothing, even if they chose to stop playing because they bought into the "you're responsible for this since you didn't stop playing" thing, I think that's a valid choice. But the issue that I see is that the story is worse if you miss events, not because there's a canonical path, but because Selebus doesn't put enough effort in following through with his alternate choices. Maybe he changes that when the game is finished, that'd be nice.

Anyone know a way to unlock all "Replays"? Just the scenes not the events. I have URM but I can't figure out the way to do it. I'm missing the last of makoto and 5th of molly and the last of ayane
Click to expand...
You need the internal name of the event. Internal names look like this: "futabalust25 - chikaspring1 - etc"
You can check the name of the scene in various ways, the one I use is to open the .rpy files in the scripts folder (there's one script folder under Game and another under Subscribestar) and look for the lines that start with "label", for example you would find "label utaspring2".
You can also see the name of the scene by going to the wiki (only for older scenes, the wiki is not being currently updated), there's a "technical data" for each event with the name of the label.
You can *also* see the scene name currently playing in the quickwatch window in URM.

Once you have the name of the scene, you go to URM to the search function, change it to search for labels/scenes and look for the scene. From there you have the option to jump to the label (that's like playing the scene for real) or replay it.

Click to expand...
I don't know if I can get on board with that in its entirety, or at least in every case. I think Sel wants to tell a story in which there are multiple options. He may want you to pick one possible path or see it as the more likely/favorable one, and some of those options may even be traps (like the shampoo,) but at the same time, the choices are there for a reason. They're also not there far more often than they are, and the story simply happens, and your role as the reader is to accept it. The story is also being told in Ren'py with those branches added in — it's not a book, and aside from choose-your-own-adventure books, books don't give you control over a character and ask "Do you want to go home or perform x?" In CYOA books, both options have an outcome — some lead to instant death, or a worse ending, or missing elements, but that's the point. I've already written about how I don't feel that missing a scene = skipping plot. It's a different plot, so those potential scenes don't happen, they're coded in for if you choose otherwise. It's not the reader altering or omitting the content, but the author creating a multitude.
I do agree that there are seemingly favorable options and options you're encouraged to choose, even more logical and fitting options. There may even be "canonical" paths, at least when the game is finished, and that's fine. I just disagree that any option is actually "losing out" so to say, and that there is no return or other gain given. And it's all still what the author decided to write and put in the game, unless retconned. Even if the purpose is to be able to fuck up the story, I think it's fitting with the story itself, one in which we constantly fuck up regardless.
Feel like I should reiterate that this is just how I feel about the story and stories with branching narratives in general, and my opinion, and doesn't equate to me saying anyone or their playthrough is wrong or that I won't be completely hardlocked out of the game in 15 months.

The recent discussion around not wanting to miss events in the wake of Io's event is interesting to me. The choices are there for a reason, and it's pretty clear that a missed event does not equate to failing an objective in, say, an FPS game. LiL frequently gives you no choice in the outcome of events, or explicitly shows you your lack of input with multiple identical options. Missable scenes, in my view, are things that could happen depending on your choices — but that does not mean you either "get" something or "don't get" something. If you miss a scene because you chose an option based on your desired outcome, you didn't lose a scene, you gained your desired outcome. Similarly, in the recent Io event, choosing the first option causes you to miss a scene — but the current scene continues and provides more dialogue, and importantly, narrative. I'd like to suggest to anyone feeling bad for missing events, ask yourself; do you want to see the event because you actually want to, or simply due to the effects of loss aversion, and would you actually gain more by interacting with the branching path mechanic with your desired outcome in mind? Something interesting for fans of the rooftop theory: Nodoka has been to the roof without Sensei.
This happens right after she transfers in, before any of her own events. So it's possible that she doesn't even start hearing voices until after going to the roof. Alternatively, the voices could have told her to go to the roof as soon as she had the chance in order to "unlock her mind" or whatever.

Context for anyone who doesn't know what the rooftop theory is:
Sensei has been able to talk to four girls (Ayane, Makoto, Tsuneyo, and Yumi) about the resets and try to get them to join the Rooftop Apocalypse Squad. These four are also the only characters that Sensei has had a scene with on the school roof, so the theory is that there is a connection between going to the roof and being able to avoid the usual forced subject change when the resets are discussed.

The roof also has special significance to Maya as she used to regularly meet Sensei there before the resets. It's possible that she was even on the roof when Sensei committed suicide ("Baby Finches"), which probably coincides with the start of the resets.

And finally, we know from Ayane that Ami has been to the roof, and we have indications that she's retaining (at least some) memories between resets and is probably able to talk about them without short-circuiting.

I believe there's a decent camp of people that think the space war isn't real, and that it is literally a gag and/or a completely random way to have an (almost) all-female setting.
If you want to rationalize it, there's a few ways you could at least attempt to. You could start by saying that generally, military tech is 10-15 years ahead of civilian/commonplace technology. You could further this by speculating that most government research funds went towards space exploration, terraforming and/or rocket technology — either before, because of, or even more-so because of worrying discoveries or alien contact. Kumon-Mi is also "outside Tokyo" (IIRC,) but we're not given much else about its economy, geography, culture, etc., or shown anywhere else. It's possible that Tokyo is partially on its way to Cyberpunk 2077, alongside places like Washington DC or Amsterdam, but Kumon-mi is not one of those leading cities when it comes to growth and economy. It might not even be Japan providing this technology in the first place, it could all be NATO or US space-faring tech, especially with their restrictions on military spending and size post WW2. Basically, Kumon-mi is a more traditional / middle-class city as opposed to a Silicon Valley, and Japan isn't on the technological forefront anyway. There's quite a difference in economy and infrastructure in Kumon-mi itself, with the old district. Considering that nearly ALL men have been drafted, this war is clearly a huge deal, and a similar thing is happening here to what happened in the world wars, where production and resources are going straight to the war, and all innovation is focused therein. Also, on the subject of the barrier, it is essentially just a big ass wall that's likely well guarded and controlled, but it could work.

In summary, Kumon-Mi is a fairly average/middle class city (with a 'poor' area) that wouldn't be modernized like Tokyo, in a country likely not on the forefront of space-faring technology, and was likely walled off near the start of the war, while production was ramping up. For whatever reason, the US, China, or whoever else was probably already investing in space travel, or even started work on colonization. Most technological innovation, funding, and resources are being concentrated solely on the war — and most of this is probably concentrated on space travel. Most countries' economies are probably being crippled because of this already. A war like that is unprecedented, and even in America in WW1/WW2 basic items and materials like metals were scarce, let alone tech.

Does the space war make sense now? I don't know, probably not. Maybe. Although if one did happen right now, in real life, it'd probably lead to a great depression worldwide on Earth, so it might be more forgivable than it seems at first.

You need the internal name of the event. Internal names look like this: "futabalust25 - chikaspring1 - etc"
You can check the name of the scene in various ways, the one I use is to open the .rpy files in the scripts folder (there's one script folder under Game and another under Subscribestar) and look for the lines that start with "label", for example you would find "label utaspring2".
You can also see the name of the scene by going to the wiki (only for older scenes, the wiki is not being currently updated), there's a "technical data" for each event with the name of the label.
You can *also* see the scene name currently playing in the quickwatch window in URM.

Once you have the name of the scene, you go to URM to the search function, change it to search for labels/scenes and look for the scene. From there you have the option to jump to the label (that's like playing the scene for real) or replay it.

You need the internal name of the event. Internal names look like this: "futabalust25 - chikaspring1 - etc"
You can check the name of the scene in various ways, the one I use is to open the .rpy files in the scripts folder (there's one script folder under Game and another under Subscribestar) and look for the lines that start with "label", for example you would find "label utaspring2".
You can also see the name of the scene by going to the wiki (only for older scenes, the wiki is not being currently updated), there's a "technical data" for each event with the name of the label.
You can *also* see the scene name currently playing in the quickwatch window in URM.
Once you have the name of the scene, you go to URM to the search function, change it to search for labels/scenes and look for the scene. From there you have the option to jump to the label (that's like playing the scene for real) or replay it.

For example, set makotofutabafuntimelustevent = TRUE and makotofutabalustskip = FALSE then the first : ( will be revealed.

Edit2: Aha I found it! set makotonodowin = TRUE to unlock the second : (

Just to throw this out there, there's something I don't think has been talked about when it comes to Io's recent events.

It wasn't necessarily about her. By that, I mean it was about Uta:
Io - "Then what were you doing with that picture of Uta?"
- "It wasn't just a misunderstanding...that was all typical wishful thinking from typical Io..."
- "I mean...what's there to even misunderstand? You're just another sick adult who can't control himself around little girls. And I'm so fucked up by now that it barely even bothers me anymore when it comes to me."
(Chapter 4's Io 'Komorebi' Event)
- "You might be telling yourself that, but you're wrong. This is going to haunt you. You're going to think about it constantly whether you want to or not...but at least it will be me instead of Uta."
(Chapter 4's Io 'Stomachache' Event)

Io looks up to Uta, and believes she would actually be dead if she never met her:
Io - "But I really look up to Uta."
- "And I probably wouldn't be here without her."
- "And I'm not joking this time, by the way."
- "I would very likely be dead if I never met Uta."
(Chapter 2's Io 'Amongst Other Things' Event)
So, it seems like Io was trying to protect Uta from Sensei, by becoming Sensei's tool, after finding out that he's holding on to a wizard pic of Uta.

In other words: Io was trying to keep him from fucking up Uta, by offering herself.

It's all she had to offer:
Io - "I won't blame you for not wanting to bathe in dirty water, Sensei. But it's all I have to offer right now."
- "This is what I was put here for."

The "parenting" stuff just forced her to stop being in denial about him. He reminded her of her mother. Then he could even use the same words she did:
Sensei - "Are you going to ignore the fact that I basically just told you I love you?"
Io - "Mhm. It's easy when you use the same words she used to."
Sensei - "That's no good. You need to relieve yourself every once in a while or you'll go crazy..."
Io - "You've gotta finish, Sensei. You need to relieve yourself every once in a while or you'll go crazy." (This seems like something she's heard before...)

In another timeline, this may have ended on a happy note:
Io - "I could do this every night for the rest of my life and not get tired of it."
- "I just hope that you're okay with me being the way I am, because I like this a lot."
But, even leaving may lead to problems. Albeit, I suppose we'll see.

I have put together some thoughts about the Io events, Its probably going to be a bit disjointed though as I don't think I have fully formed my thoughts on it yet. Some of it is similar to what DeSkel15 just posted. And I do hope it does not come off as reductive of insensitive for whatever reason.

To start with just some thoughts on the way Io has been written and other general stuff that came to mind:
I do really like the way Io’s character has seemingly been deliberately constructed in such a way that there is a high chance you don't like her very much going into the event chain in this update. I think it's genius writing from Selebus.
It hits you so hard when you have everything about her past dropped on you while not really liking her. It makes you feel terrible when everything she said or did in the past that made you dislike her is explained in a way that so immediately makes all those actions so understandable. It pulls you into the scene in a way, makes you feel like you are also an asshole for disliking her for all those various things. I felt it made it a lot more impactful and added so much to the feeling of despair I had for her by the end of it all.

Also the cinematography in the Io events is very good. Selebus has always been good at using facial expressions and body language, but I feel like he combined it very well with camera angle and framing choices in this update. Maybe it's been good for a while and I'm just noticing it consciously now for some reason, but it stood out to me in this update (2nd Noriko event as well).
And now some possible observations and interpretations on Io's motivations/state of mind.(probably too many images)
I don't think ill be able to structure this very well so ill just post most of the images first. Then give you a text block that hopefully will make sense and does not misconstrue what I'm thinking.
there is these lines from "Amongst Other Things":




then this line from her about Uta:

And these lines from Uta in the current update give a bit of an insight about part of what's probably going through Io's mind.

then there is all this from the event.
















Through Io's events she goes through this progression of offering Akira more of herself, thinking maybe it's the only way to keep him interested in her / appease him (she already knows he is a groomer from early on). It starts with; I cant do anything, then gets to I might be able to deal with kissing, then she says I can deal with being there while you do things with someone else (Uta).

In the events in this update she seems to come to the conclusion that uta is no longer an option she can use to avoid Akira's lust. (because of the photo he has of Uta Io expects Uta to hate Akira now). Additionally In thinking Uta now hates Akira she wants to protect Uta from Akira Because she could not live with herself if Uta got hurt in some way for the sake of Io and Akira's relationship.

She comes to a point where she does not care about herself anymore, but she still wants to keep Akira around. Without the Uta option she thinks she will have to appease his lust herself for that to even be a possibility after the argument and shared revelations about their pasts. She says keeping him around is about survival. She previously said if things failed with him "I'll probably just die".

So she seems to goes through with this partly to protect Uta from him. Partly because she thinks It's the only way to stop him from never talking to her again. And partly because she has given up on everything (thinks she is just going to kill herself?) if he never talks to her again. So she just resigns herself to endure him in hope that on the other side of it there is a possibility to continue some kind of a relationship with him. In the moment Io seems to truly believe that if she does not give him what she believes he wants it is over with him.

I guess the main quotes from her are these:
“If things don't work out with you, I’ll probably just die…You really are my last line of defence”
"this isn't about gaining anything. It's about survival"
"At first, I thought you might be able to save me. Now, I just don't know what else to do with myself."
"but at least it will be me instead of Uta."

DeSkel15 said:
Just to throw this out there, there's something I don't think has been talked about when it comes to Io's recent events.

It wasn't necessarily about her. By that, I mean it was about Uta:
View attachment 3806836 View attachment 3806835 View attachment 3806767 View attachment 3806768 Io - "Then what were you doing with that picture of Uta?"
- "It wasn't just a misunderstanding...that was all typical wishful thinking from typical Io..."
- "I mean...what's there to even misunderstand? You're just another sick adult who can't control himself around little girls. And I'm so fucked up by now that it barely even bothers me anymore when it comes to me."
(Chapter 4's Io 'Komorebi' Event)
- "You might be telling yourself that, but you're wrong. This is going to haunt you. You're going to think about it constantly whether you want to or not...but at least it will be me instead of Uta."
(Chapter 4's Io 'Stomachache' Event)

Io looks up to Uta, and believes she would actually be dead if she never met her:
View attachment 3806771 View attachment 3806773 View attachment 3806776 View attachment 3806778 Io - "But I really look up to Uta."
- "And I probably wouldn't be here without her."
- "And I'm not joking this time, by the way."
- "I would very likely be dead if I never met Uta."
(Chapter 2's Io 'Amongst Other Things' Event)
So, it seems like Io was trying to protect Uta from Sensei, by becoming Sensei's tool, after finding out that he's holding on to a wizard pic of Uta.

In other words: Io was trying to keep him from fucking up Uta, by offering herself.

It's all she had to offer:
View attachment 3806783 View attachment 3806785 Io - "I won't blame you for not wanting to bathe in dirty water, Sensei. But it's all I have to offer right now."
- "This is what I was put here for."

The "parenting" stuff just forced her to stop being in denial about him. He reminded her of her mother. Then he could even use the same words she did:
View attachment 3806787 View attachment 3806789 View attachment 3806790 View attachment 3806791 Sensei - "Are you going to ignore the fact that I basically just told you I love you?"
Io - "Mhm. It's easy when you use the same words she used to."
Sensei - "That's no good. You need to relieve yourself every once in a while or you'll go crazy..."
Io - "You've gotta finish, Sensei. You need to relieve yourself every once in a while or you'll go crazy." (This seems like something she's heard before...)

In another timeline, this may have ended on a happy note:
View attachment 3806802 View attachment 3806803 Io - "I could do this every night for the rest of my life and not get tired of it."
- "I just hope that you're okay with me being the way I am, because I like this a lot."
But, even leaving may lead to problems. Albeit, I suppose we'll see.
Click to expand...
I have not said that, but everything I said about it fits very well with this. By that I mean that Io spearheaded the whole conversation, shot down every Akira attempt to disengage, and was overall dead-set on it happening. Also that she was out of her mind the whole time since the moment Akira tried to justify Ami being important to him by using a comparison. All of those fit with her being on a mission.

I don't think Uta was the sole reason, since if it was, Io would be incredibly misguided (if not stupid). Uta never needed this help, since Akira being the way he is is ultimately good for her. Uta herself says that, in prior conversations with Io, it was Io that seemed intent on Uta dealing with this news in a manner that was very different from what she seemed to take from it. But I think we can all agree that Io wasn't thinking straight, and that in that sense protecting Uta was certainly part of it, since she said it herself (it just doesn't doesn't match with reality, but then again, barely anything about the stomachace conversation matches with reality because Io hardly listens to Akira).

I think there's a chance Io won't be ruined from this, but I think it would be interesting/ironic/tragic for her to be ruined form realising that her efforts were absolutely misguided. Uta never needed her "protection", and Akira, having been molested as well, would never have left her because of that. In that case, either she went through with it for no reason, or she "tarnished" herself by vomiting her entire backstory on him, pressuring him to have sex (which he refuses), and ultimately she would also have put herself in that position for no reason. Selebus might choose that route to link both options.

Unintended though they may have been however, Io's events had one important repercussion, which was the way Akira handled Uta's conversation. Uta already didn't have much of a problem with it, and was really just confirming. But the fact that Akira breaks down in front of her definitely makes Uta's decision easier, as she can relate better to someone that displays being actively broken about these issues than if Akira had been more composed (like it was not a problem for him).

If the timeline was also reversed, I think it lends credence to your take, because if during the conversation Akira had been "Io, Uta's fine with it, we already talked" - Io would be hard-pressed not to slow down. I don't know that she'd give up, but it would definitely change things (just as Akira's Sekai's reveal forces her to slow down as well). In that same token, if Akira had actively broken down in front of her, that would probably have also changed things.

As it is, Io was dealt a bad hand and made sure to make the worst of it. And in doing so, she ended up providing Uta and whoever came later with a better hand by default.

On a final note, a wonder to which extent the world itself/whoever speaks to Nodoka foresaw/intended for this event so that Akira could reveal Sekai to someone for the first time:
The event is called "trauma bond", Akira is the only one that would have the same trauma as Io, and what Nodoka says can be completed as "spilling traumautic events from a character's past would serve no purpose other than to serve as trigger to have the protagonist talk to them about it in a one-on-one conversation later". Which is what she tried to do, but was rejected, and that served as a trigger for Akira to have the conversation she wanted to have. If not for Nodoka, even with Uta's picture, Io's events would never have happened. Was that happenstance however? Or was it by design?

I have not said that, but everything I said about it fits very well with this. By that I mean that Io spearheaded the whole conversation, shot down every Akira attempt to disengage, and was overall dead-set on it happening. Also that she was out of her mind the whole time since the moment Akira tried to justify Ami being important to him by using a comparison. All of those fit with her being on a mission.
I don't think Uta was the sole reason, since if it was, Io would be incredibly misguided (if not stupid). Uta never needed this help, since Akira being the way he is is ultimately good for her. Uta herself says that, in prior conversations with Io, it was Io that seemed intent on Uta dealing with this news in a manner that was very different from what she seemed to take from it. But I think we can all agree that Io wasn't thinking straight, and that in that sense protecting Uta was certainly part of it, since she said it herself (it just doesn't doesn't match with reality, but then again, barely anything about the stomachace conversation matches with reality because Io hardly listens to Akira).
I think there's a chance Io won't be ruined from this, but I think it would be interesting/ironic/tragic for her to be ruined form realising that her efforts were absolutely misguided. Uta never needed her "protection", and Akira, having been molested as well, would never have left her because of that. In that case, either she went through with it for no reason, or she "tarnished" herself by vomiting her entire backstory on him, pressuring him to have sex (which he refuses), and ultimately she would also have put herself in that position for no reason. Selebus might choose that route to link both options.
Unintended though they may have been however, Io's events had one important repercussion, which was the way Akira handled Uta's conversation. Uta already didn't have much of a problem with it, and was really just confirming. But the fact that Akira breaks down in front of her definitely makes Uta's decision easier, as she can relate better to someone that displays being actively broken about these issues than if Akira had been more composed (like it was not a problem for him).
If the timeline was also reversed, I think it lends credence to your take, because if during the conversation Akira had been "Io, Uta's fine with it, we already talked" - Io would be hard-pressed not to slow down. I don't know that she'd give up, but it would definitely change things (just as Akira's Sekai's reveal forces her to slow down as well). In that same token, if Akira had actively broken down in front of her, that would probably have also changed things.
As it is, Io was dealt a bad hand and made sure to make the worst of it. And in doing so, she ended up providing Uta and whoever came later with a better hand by default.
On a final note, a wonder to which extent the world itself/whoever speaks to Nodoka foresaw/intended for this event so that Akira could reveal Sekai to someone for the first time:
Spoiler:
trauma bond
The event is called "trauma bond", Akira is the only one that would have the same trauma as Io, and what Nodoka says can be completed as "spilling traumautic events from a character's past would serve no purpose other than to
serve as trigger to have the protagonist talk to them about it in a one-on-one conversation later
". Which is what she tried to do, but was rejected, and that served as a trigger for Akira to have the conversation she wanted to have. If not for Nodoka, even with Uta's picture, Io's events would never have happened. Was that happenstance however? Or was it by design?

Who do you think would have the worst reaction out of the adults? I'd say Wakana or Osako, maybe Sara. Pretty sure it would be Chika out of the students. Of course there would be two different things to react to, him sleeping with his students and him sleeping with his daughterniece.
Click to expand...
Let's see, of the adults, I think Osako knows about Ayane at the very least. But she's in a unique position that she can just not care, since she's not involved with either Akira or the school. And from her point of view, it's clearly "consensual" - so it's not like she's abandoning a victim. I think Niki is more or less the same, she knows Akira wouldn't go forcing himself on anyone, and would rather not know about it (since she can't abandon him, so the less she knows the better) - also because the highest possibility to her is her own sister, who would more than willingly have sex with him.

Sara is in a unique situation because she knows about/had the blackouts and had a relationship with her teacher. I think she'd be the most accepting of it overall. Not accepting in a Haruka way, but accepting in a "I get it, it's out of your control". Tbh it makes it much easier to accept whatever Akira does if the supernatural is involved, and Sara is in that position of not even having to be convinced, she actually lived it. Would she accept it turning into an oyakodon situation with Sana? You know what? I don't know... And that's more than we should be able to say about most people. I think it's possible, as long as Akira actually stuck with them. We may see a situation in which Akira has children from both mother and daughter, and they're both siblings and aunt/uncle of eachother. That'd be interesting by itself.

Now, ironically enough, to "normal" adults. Maki would freak and probably be appaled by it - at least concerning Makoto. Concerning the other teenagers, I don't know. I think she might sort of give him a pass if it was one teenager. I think a lot of people would give him a pass in that case to be honest. As to Wakana, oh boy. That's a difficult question. Normally, Wakana should be the most appaled. But then Wakana cares deeply for him, and understands where it comes from. I think she's way too deep to pull out now, and would probably fall into a "I can fix him" situation if push came to shove. It's a bit weird that Osako hasn't straight up told her about Ayane though - I guess it just goes to show how Akira doesn't even show up in her radar as a threat.

Edit: A funny thought, but it would be interesting if Yuki didn't approve of it because Akira is not including Yumi in it. And a less funny but actually possible thought is that Yuki is trying to keep herself away from her feelings for him because she's able to see that Yumi likes him.
I think most of the students know to be honest. Maybe the right question is what if they found out he has sex with Ami, or that he started having sex with Maya when she was a wizard. That would probably be a shock to them. For the Ami situation, after her recent antics, they'd probably rationalize it as it being an Ami thing though. That's how low her cred has fallen. And the wizard thing is hard to react to, the Uta photo was a very unique case. If he has sex with Tsukasa though, then I think everyone out of Nodoka, Yasu and the rooftop squad would abandon him. I don't think even Noriko would stay with him, but then again maybe she enters RAS (and they'll never abandon him regardless).

The one person from the students that thinks they're exclusive is Chika. And I guess technically Ami - but let's get real, there is no way she doesn't know by now, at least regarding Maya. Let's check:

From the teenagers physically involved with Akira (willingly or not): Chika (sex), Yumi (forced kiss), Ayane (sex), Sana (oral), Makoto (sex), Miku (oral), Futaba (sex), Rin (kiss on good homie), Ami (sex), Maya (sex), Molly (oral), Io (sex), Nodoka (sex), Yasu (orgasms under possession), Noriko (fingering), Kirin (sex) - Chika is the only one that doesn't know about someone else.

From the teenagers not involved: Tsuneyo, Uta (about to), Otoha, Touka (about to) - it's possible that Tsuneyo doesn't have evidence, but she has seen worse.

So yeah, definitely Chika would react the worst. And I hope she does soon.

Simple answer: Probably Maki from the adults, and Chika from the teenagers. Wakana cares too much about Akira by now that she'd try to fix him instead.

Oooo spoilers? Gimme gimme? That game is finally almost complete and i can soon jump back into it and finish it off... now gimme spoilers!
Click to expand...
I mean, I played the public build - it's out. But, basically:
A lot of spoilers for the final battle.

You go to battle in the tower. That old lady (that trapped the goddess) is racing against the remaining incubus king (the one that is all about order and stuff), I totally forgot their names. The tower is like a bunch of bases around one central base. The more bases you control, the easier it should be to break the door at the center. And by breaching that door, you can get to the manifestation of destiny itself, or something to that effect.

There are some tactics that you employ, cause you lead the teams made from your party members, but you also have some people that act alone, and they have a limited stamina stat. Use too much and you can't prevent things when/if tragedy strikes. usual TLS stuff. So you start battling for the bases, and a lot of stuff happens depending on your employed tactics and overall state of the world. They may send reinforcements for instance. At one point Takan (?), the orc country sent a strike team and they sacrificed themselves to buy me time. At another, the hero orc team protected the orc maker lady. At one point Ginasta clearly could have prevented disaster, but didn't cause I guess my affection wasn't high enough with her.

There is a moment in which the goddesses choose avatars to make themselves immune to corruption. I didn't fail anything other than the Ginasta stuff, and it would be really tragic if the goddess of magic fell to lust when being tempted by an incubus king (cause that happens at one point), but she resisted in my playthrough cause she was aided by her followers. Well, there are too many minor things to list them all, and I also just played once, so maybe there are many things I didn't find depending on my decisions. My favorite minor moment is when the succubus holy knights show up though, they look really cool.

But the point I made reference to is the end of the battle in which Yarra turns into Goku (from dragon ball), and calls upon the entire world for them to send her energy. No cap she makes a genki dama, a big ball of energy, and just so Sierra isn't copyright struck, she also starts to get lust energy from people helping. So instead of making one big ball of energy, she makes two, which is basically a set of boobs. Then she throws them at the enemy and that's it, you win.

Current build ends with a long discussion with everyone involved about either taking control of fate or becoming its guardians (so no one takes control of it). I don't know if there will be an actual choice here, because the dialogue ends with everyone sort of agreeing to becoming gods, but stopping any interference after one lifetime worth of it. So basically change the world for the next 100 years, and then retire somewhere. I hope there's some choice, but we'll see.

Now, I wouldn't say it was underwhelming, but I thought it wasn't exactly my favorite battle sequence. Of course, it's lacking its actual consequences so maybe that's it. Gotta wait for the epilogues now, and also the walkthroughs cause god it was awful to play without it.
